jab.t:
v. 猛戳；快速刺出
n. 戳；注射

e.en: He gave the punching bag a quick {jab}.
e.zh: 他朝沙袋快速地刺了一拳。

e.en: Millions lined up to receive their first COVID {jab}.
e.zh: 数百万人排队接种第一针新冠疫苗。

jabber.t:
v. 叽里咕噜地说
n. 急促的话

e.en: The toddlers {jabber} excitedly during snack time.
e.zh: 孩子们在吃点心时叽里呱啦地说个不停。

e.en: Stop your {jabber} and listen to the instructions.
e.zh: 别再唠叨了,听一下说明。

e.en: Purple {jacaranda} blossoms covered the streets in spring.
e.zh: 春天里紫色的蓝花楹覆盖了整条街道。

e.en: A huge {jacaranda} tree shaded their backyard.
e.zh: 一棵巨大的蓝花楹为他们的后院遮阴。

jack.t:
n. 千斤顶；插孔
v. 用千斤顶顶起

e.en: Use the car {jack} to lift the vehicle safely.
e.zh: 用千斤顶安全地把车顶起来。

e.en: Plug the headphones into the audio {jack}.
e.zh: 把耳机插入音频插孔。

e.en: A lone {jackal} crossed the dusty trail at dusk.
e.zh: 黄昏时,一只孤独的豺穿过尘土飞扬的小径。

e.en: The {jackal} scavenged scraps left by the lions.
e.zh: 那只豺以狮子吃剩的残渣为食。

e.en: Don't be a {jackass} and apologize to her.
e.zh: 别像个混蛋一样,跟她道个歉。

e.en: A stubborn {jackass} blocked the narrow mountain path.
e.zh: 一头倔强的驴堵住了狭窄的山路。

jackboot.t: n. 长筒军靴；高压统治

e.en: The polished {jackboot} symbolized the regime's brutal authority.
e.zh: 那双锃亮的长筒军靴象征着政权的残暴权威。

e.en: He shined his {jackboot} until it gleamed.
e.zh: 他把长筒军靴擦得锃亮发光。

jackbooted.t: adj. 穿长筒军靴的；高压专横的

e.en: {Jackbooted} soldiers marched through the captured city.
e.zh: 穿着长筒军靴的士兵在被占领的城市中行进。

e.en: Critics called the policy {jackbooted} authoritarianism.
e.zh: 批评者称这项政策是专横霸道的强权统治。

e.en: A noisy {jackdaw} perched on the chimney pot.
e.zh: 一只吵闹的寒鸦停在烟囱口上。

e.en: The {jackdaw} stole shiny objects from the windowsill.
e.zh: 那只寒鸦从窗台上偷走亮闪闪的小物件。

e.en: Grab your {jacket} before heading out into the cold.
e.zh: 出门前记得把外套穿上,外面很冷。

e.en: The book's dust {jacket} features beautiful artwork.
e.zh: 这本书的护封上印有精美的插画。

jacketed.t: adj. 穿着夹克的；带护套的

e.en: The leather-{jacketed} riders revved their motorcycles loudly.
e.zh: 穿皮夹克的骑手大声轰着摩托车油门。

e.en: A water-{jacketed} reactor maintains a stable temperature.
e.zh: 带水套的反应器能保持温度稳定。

e.en: Winter {jackets} are on sale this weekend.
e.zh: 冬季外套这个周末特价促销。

e.en: The hikers stuffed their {jackets} into their backpacks.
e.zh: 徒步者把外套塞进了背包里。

e.en: Ripe {jackfruit} smells sweet and fills the kitchen.
e.zh: 熟透的菠萝蜜散发出甜香,弥漫整个厨房。

e.en: Many vegans use {jackfruit} as a meat substitute.
e.zh: 许多素食者把菠萝蜜当作肉类替代品。

e.en: A noisy {jackhammer} woke me up at dawn.
e.zh: 一台嘈杂的风钻在清晨把我吵醒。

e.en: The worker used a {jackhammer} to break the concrete.
e.zh: 工人用风钻把混凝土打碎。

jackknife.t:
n. 大折刀
v. (车) 折叠式打滑

e.en: He whittled the stick with a small {jackknife}.
e.zh: 他用一把小折刀削着木棍。

e.en: The diver performed a perfect {jackknife} into the pool.
e.zh: 那位跳水者完美地做了一个屈体跳水入池。

e.en: She won the {jackpot} on her very first spin.
e.zh: 她第一把摇奖就中了头奖。

e.en: This new client is a real {jackpot} for our agency.
e.zh: 这位新客户对我们公司来说真是个大单子。

e.en: A startled {jackrabbit} darted across the desert highway.
e.zh: 一只受惊的长耳大野兔窜过沙漠公路。

e.en: The dog chased the {jackrabbit} into the tall grass.
e.zh: 狗把那只长耳大野兔追进了高高的草丛里。

e.en: Mechanics replaced the worn {jackscrew} on the aircraft's tail.
e.zh: 机械师更换了飞机尾翼上磨损的螺旋千斤顶。

e.en: A heavy-duty {jackscrew} can lift several tons easily.
e.zh: 重型螺旋千斤顶可以轻松举起数吨重物。

e.en: Michael {Jackson} remains one of pop music's biggest icons.
e.zh: 迈克尔·杰克逊至今仍是流行音乐最伟大的偶像之一。

e.en: {Jackson} is the capital city of Mississippi.
e.zh: 杰克逊是密西西比州的首府。

jacksonian.t: adj. 杰克逊式的（美国总统派系）

e.en: {Jacksonian} democracy expanded voting rights for white men.
e.zh: 杰克逊式民主扩大了白人男性的选举权。

e.en: Historians still debate the legacy of the {Jacksonian} era.
e.zh: 历史学家至今仍在讨论杰克逊时代的遗产。

jacksonville.t: n. 杰克逊维尔（美国城市）

e.en: We flew to {Jacksonville} for the football game last weekend.
e.zh: 上周末我们飞去杰克逊维尔看橄榄球比赛。

e.en: {Jacksonville} is the largest city by area in Florida.
e.zh: 杰克逊维尔是佛罗里达州面积最大的城市。

e.en: {Jacob} just got promoted to senior engineer at his startup.
e.zh: 雅各布刚刚在他的创业公司晋升为高级工程师。

e.en: The story of {Jacob} appears in the Book of Genesis.
e.zh: 雅各的故事出现在《创世记》中。

jacobean.t: adj. 英王詹姆斯一世时期的

e.en: The mansion features a beautifully preserved {Jacobean} staircase.
e.zh: 这座宅邸有一座保存完好的詹姆斯一世时期楼梯。

e.en: She specializes in {Jacobean} drama and revenge tragedies.
e.zh: 她专攻詹姆斯一世时期的戏剧和复仇悲剧。

jacobin.t: n. 雅各宾派（法国大革命）

e.en: The {Jacobin} club dominated French politics during the Revolution.
e.zh: 雅各宾俱乐部在法国大革命期间主导了政治。

e.en: Critics called the reformers radical {Jacobins} bent on chaos.
e.zh: 批评者称这些改革者是一心制造混乱的激进雅各宾派。

e.en: The {Jacobite} rebellion of 1745 ended at Culloden.
e.zh: 1745年的詹姆斯党起义在卡洛登战役中结束。

e.en: His ancestors were loyal {Jacobites} who fled to France.
e.zh: 他的祖先是忠诚的詹姆斯党人,逃到了法国。

jacobitism.t: n. 詹姆斯二世党人主义

e.en: {Jacobitism} faded after the defeat at Culloden in 1746.
e.zh: 1746年卡洛登战败后,詹姆斯党主义逐渐消亡。

e.en: The professor wrote a book about Scottish {Jacobitism}.
e.zh: 这位教授写了一本关于苏格兰詹姆斯党主义的书。

jacquard.t: n. 提花织物；提花织机

e.en: She wore a stunning {jacquard} jacket to the gala.
e.zh: 她穿着一件惊艳的提花外套出席晚会。

e.en: The {jacquard} loom revolutionized textile manufacturing in the 1800s.
e.zh: 提花织机在19世纪彻底革新了纺织业。

e.en: After skiing all day, we soaked in the hotel {jacuzzi}.
e.zh: 滑了一天雪后,我们泡进了酒店的按摩浴缸。

e.en: Their backyard has a heated {jacuzzi} under the stars.
e.zh: 他们后院有一个星空下的加热按摩浴缸。

jade.t:
n. 玉；翡翠
adj. 翠绿色的

e.en: Her grandmother gave her a beautiful {jade} bracelet.
e.zh: 她奶奶送了她一只漂亮的玉手镯。

e.en: The lake's water was a striking shade of {jade}.
e.zh: 湖水呈现出醒目的翡翠色。

e.en: After ten years in the industry, he sounds completely {jaded}.
e.zh: 在这行干了十年后,他听起来彻底厌倦了。

e.en: Even {jaded} critics praised the film's emotional ending.
e.zh: 就连厌倦的影评人也称赞了这部电影的感人结局。

e.en: The museum displayed a rare {jadeite} carving from Myanmar.
e.zh: 博物馆展出了一件来自缅甸的稀有硬玉雕刻。

e.en: Burmese {jadeite} commands the highest prices at auction.
e.zh: 缅甸硬玉在拍卖会上能拍出最高价。

e.en: The collector keeps several antique {jades} in a glass case.
e.zh: 这位收藏家在玻璃柜里放着几件古玉。

e.en: Endless meetings {jades} even the most enthusiastic employees.
e.zh: 无休止的会议会让最热情的员工也心生厌倦。

e.en: A {jaeger} circled overhead, looking to steal another bird's catch.
e.zh: 一只贼鸥在头顶盘旋,想抢夺别的鸟的猎物。

e.en: He ordered a shot of {Jaeger} at the bar.
e.zh: 他在酒吧点了一杯野格酒。

jaffa.t: n. 雅法（以色列城市）；雅法橙

e.en: We bought fresh {Jaffa} oranges at the local market.
e.zh: 我们在当地市场买了新鲜的雅法橙。

e.en: The old port of {Jaffa} blends ancient stone with modern cafes.
e.zh: 古老的雅法港把古老石墙和现代咖啡馆融为一体。

jag.t:
n. 尖齿；锯齿
n. 一阵（狂欢、哭闹等）

e.en: He went on a shopping {jag} after his promotion.
e.zh: 升职之后他疯狂购物了一阵。

e.en: A sharp {jag} of lightning split the night sky.
e.zh: 一道锯齿状的闪电划破了夜空。

jagged.t: adj. 锯齿状的；参差不齐的

e.en: The hikers carefully climbed the {jagged} mountain ridge.
e.zh: 徒步者小心地攀登那道参差不齐的山脊。

e.en: Broken glass left a {jagged} edge along the windowsill.
e.zh: 碎玻璃在窗台上留下了一道锯齿状的边缘。

jaggedly.t: adv. 参差不齐地；锯齿状地

e.en: The cliff dropped {jaggedly} into the foaming sea below.
e.zh: 悬崖参差不齐地直插入下方翻腾的海水。

e.en: She breathed {jaggedly} after sprinting up the stairs.
e.zh: 她冲上楼梯后呼吸断断续续。

jagger.t: n. 贾格尔（姓氏，如 Mick Jagger）

e.en: Mick {Jagger} still performs with incredible energy at his age.
e.zh: 米克·贾格尔这个年纪登台依旧活力惊人。

e.en: The biopic explores {Jagger}'s rise to global rock stardom.
e.zh: 这部传记片讲述了贾格尔成长为全球摇滚巨星的过程。

jaguar.t: n. 美洲豹；捷豹（汽车品牌）

e.en: A {jaguar} prowled silently through the dense Amazon rainforest.
e.zh: 一只美洲豹悄无声息地穿过茂密的亚马逊雨林。

e.en: He drives a vintage {Jaguar} restored to perfect condition.
e.zh: 他开着一辆修复得完美如初的老款捷豹。

jail.t:
n. 监狱
v. 监禁

e.en: The judge sent him to {jail} for six months.
e.zh: 法官判他坐六个月的牢。

e.en: Reformers want to reduce overcrowding in the county {jail}.
e.zh: 改革者希望减轻县监狱的拥挤状况。

e.en: The novel's protagonist is a reformed {jailbird} seeking redemption.
e.zh: 小说主角是一名寻求救赎的改过自新的牢友。

e.en: Don't call him a {jailbird}—he served his time honestly.
e.zh: 别叫他囚犯,他已经诚实地服完了刑。

jailbreak.t: n. 越狱（也指破解系统限制）

e.en: The {jailbreak} made headlines across the country that morning.
e.zh: 那场越狱当天上午登上了全国各大头条。

e.en: Hackers found a clever {jailbreak} for the new chatbot.
e.zh: 黑客们找到了一种巧妙的方法绕过新聊天机器人的限制。

jailed.t: v. 监禁（过去式/过去分词）

e.en: The activist was {jailed} for protesting outside parliament.
e.zh: 那位活动人士因在议会外抗议而被关进监狱。

e.en: Several executives were {jailed} after the fraud investigation.
e.zh: 欺诈调查结束后,几名高管被判入狱。

e.en: The {jailer} unlocked the cell and waved the visitor inside.
e.zh: 狱卒打开牢门,挥手示意访客进去。

e.en: She felt like her own anxiety had become her {jailer}.
e.zh: 她觉得自己的焦虑已经成了禁锢自己的狱卒。

e.en: He learned to play guitar during his time in the {jailhouse}.
e.zh: 他在监狱期间学会了弹吉他。

e.en: The detective used a classic {jailhouse} interrogation tactic.
e.zh: 那位侦探用了经典的监狱审讯手法。

e.en: Critics oppose {jailing} nonviolent offenders for minor drug crimes.
e.zh: 批评者反对因轻微毒品犯罪而监禁非暴力罪犯。

e.en: The country faced backlash for {jailing} journalists without trial.
e.zh: 该国因不经审判监禁记者而遭到强烈反对。

jails.t:
n. 监狱（复数）
v. 监禁（第三人称单数）

e.en: Many local {jails} are dangerously overcrowded this year.
e.zh: 今年许多地方监狱拥挤到了危险的程度。

e.en: The dictator routinely {jails} political opponents without charges.
e.zh: 那位独裁者经常不经指控就把政敌投入监狱。

jain.t:
n. 耆那教徒
adj. 耆那教的

e.en: My {Jain} neighbors strictly avoid eating root vegetables.
e.zh: 我的耆那教邻居严格不吃根茎类蔬菜。

e.en: The {Jain} temple in Mumbai is famous for its marble carvings.
e.zh: 孟买的耆那教寺庙以其大理石雕刻闻名。

e.en: We spent three days exploring the pink palaces of {Jaipur}.
e.zh: 我们花了三天时间游览斋浦尔的粉色宫殿。

e.en: {Jaipur} is famous for its handmade textiles and gemstones.
e.zh: 斋浦尔以手工纺织品和宝石闻名。

e.en: The flight to {Jakarta} takes about seven hours from Tokyo.
e.zh: 从东京飞往雅加达大约需要七个小时。

e.en: {Jakarta} struggles with traffic congestion and rising sea levels.
e.zh: 雅加达正在与交通拥堵和海平面上升作斗争。

jake.t:
n. 杰克（男子名）
adj. 美俚 没问题的

e.en: {Jake} just texted that he's running ten minutes late.
e.zh: 杰克刚发消息说他要迟到十分钟。

e.en: Don't worry, everything is {jake} between us now.
e.zh: 别担心,我们之间现在一切都好。

e.en: The old farmhouse still had a {jakes} out back.
e.zh: 那座老农舍后头还有一间老式茅厕。

e.en: Shakespeare's characters occasionally joke about visiting the {jakes}.
e.zh: 莎士比亚笔下的角色偶尔会拿上茅厕开玩笑。

e.en: She topped her nachos with sliced {jalapeno} peppers.
e.zh: 她在玉米片上撒了切片的墨西哥辣椒。

e.en: This salsa is too spicy—they used way too much {jalapeno}.
e.zh: 这莎莎酱太辣了,他们放了太多墨西哥辣椒。

e.en: He drove an old {jalopy} that broke down every other week.
e.zh: 他开着一辆隔三差五就抛锚的破旧老车。

e.en: That rusty {jalopy} somehow still passes its annual inspection.
e.zh: 那辆生锈的破车不知怎的每年都能通过年检。

jam.t:
n. 果酱；堵塞
v. 塞满；卡住

e.en: I spread strawberry {jam} on my toast every morning.
e.zh: 我每天早上在吐司上抹草莓酱。

e.en: We were stuck in a traffic {jam} for two hours.
e.zh: 我们在堵车里困了两个小时。

jamaica.t: n. 牙买加（加勒比海国家）

e.en: They honeymooned in {Jamaica} and loved every minute of it.
e.zh: 他们去牙买加度蜜月,每一刻都很享受。

e.en: {Jamaica} is famous worldwide for reggae music and Blue Mountain coffee.
e.zh: 牙买加因雷鬼音乐和蓝山咖啡享誉世界。

jamaican.t:
adj. 牙买加的
n. 牙买加人

e.en: The {Jamaican} restaurant on the corner serves amazing jerk chicken.
e.zh: 街角那家牙买加餐厅的烟熏鸡非常好吃。

e.en: Bob Marley remains the most famous {Jamaican} musician ever.
e.zh: 鲍勃·马利依然是有史以来最著名的牙买加音乐人。

e.en: He leaned against the door {jamb} while we talked.
e.zh: 我们说话时他靠在门框上。

e.en: The carpenter replaced the rotten window {jamb} yesterday.
e.zh: 昨天木匠换掉了腐烂的窗框侧柱。

jambalaya.t: n. 什锦饭（美国南方菜）

e.en: Her Cajun {jambalaya} recipe has been in the family for generations.
e.zh: 她的卡津什锦饭食谱在家族里传了好几代。

e.en: We ordered {jambalaya} and gumbo at the New Orleans diner.
e.zh: 我们在新奥尔良那家小馆点了什锦饭和秋葵浓汤。

jamboree.t: n. 大型联欢会；童子军大会

e.en: The scouts gathered for a weekend {jamboree} in the mountains.
e.zh: 童子军们聚在山里过了一个周末的大会。

e.en: The annual music {jamboree} draws thousands of fans every July.
e.zh: 每年七月的音乐大会都吸引数千名乐迷。

e.en: {James} sent the report to his manager just before noon.
e.zh: 詹姆斯在中午前把报告发给了他的经理。

e.en: King {James} commissioned a famous English Bible translation in 1611.
e.zh: 詹姆斯王在1611年下令翻译了那本著名的英文版圣经。

jamesian.t: adj. 詹姆斯式的（关于亨利·詹姆斯或威廉·詹姆斯）

e.en: The novel's introspective style is distinctly {Jamesian}.
e.zh: 这部小说的内省风格明显带有亨利·詹姆斯的特色。

e.en: Critics noted the {Jamesian} ambiguity in her short stories.
e.zh: 评论家指出她短篇小说里有亨利·詹姆斯式的模糊感。

jameson.t: n. 詹姆森（姓氏；爱尔兰威士忌品牌）

e.en: He poured himself a glass of {Jameson} after work.
e.zh: 下班后他给自己倒了一杯尊美醇威士忌。

e.en: The bartender recommended {Jameson} on the rocks.
e.zh: 调酒师推荐尊美醇加冰。

jammed.t:
adj. 卡住的；堵塞的
v. jam 的过去式

e.en: The printer {jammed} again right before the meeting.
e.zh: 打印机在会议前又卡纸了。

e.en: The stadium was {jammed} with screaming fans on Saturday night.
e.zh: 周六晚上体育场里挤满了尖叫的粉丝。

e.en: Police seized an illegal signal {jammer} from the suspect's car.
e.zh: 警方从嫌疑人的车里查获了一台非法信号干扰器。

e.en: The {jammer} blocked all cell phone calls inside the secure room.
e.zh: 那台干扰器屏蔽了安全室内所有手机通话。

e.en: The kids put on their {jammies} and brushed their teeth.
e.zh: 孩子们穿上睡衣,刷了牙。

e.en: On Sundays I stay in my {jammies} until noon.
e.zh: 周日我会一直穿着睡衣到中午。

jamming.t:
n. 信号干扰
v. 卡住；即兴演奏

e.en: The band spent the afternoon {jamming} in the garage.
e.zh: 乐队整个下午都在车库里即兴演奏。

e.en: Russia was accused of {jamming} GPS signals across the border.
e.zh: 俄罗斯被指控在边境干扰GPS信号。

e.en: We took a train from Delhi to {Jammu} last summer.
e.zh: 去年夏天我们从德里坐火车去了查谟。

e.en: {Jammu} and Kashmir has stunning mountain scenery.
e.zh: 查谟和克什米尔有壮丽的山地风光。

jammy.t:
adj. 走运的（英式口语）
adj. 果酱状的

e.en: You're so {jammy}—you found parking right outside the venue.
e.zh: 你也太走运了,在场馆门口就找到了停车位。

e.en: This wine has a rich, {jammy} blackberry flavor.
e.zh: 这款酒有浓郁的、像果酱般的黑莓味。

jams.t:
n. 果酱
v. 塞入；卡住

e.en: My grandmother makes the best homemade {jams} every summer.
e.zh: 我奶奶每年夏天做的自制果酱是最好吃的。

e.en: The DJ played all the classic {jams} from the nineties.
e.zh: DJ播放了九十年代所有经典的劲歌。

e.en: The report is due by the end of {Jan} next year.
e.zh: 报告必须在明年一月底前提交。

e.en: My friend {Jan} just moved to Berlin for work.
e.zh: 我的朋友扬刚搬到柏林工作。

janata.t: n. 人民（印地语）；印度人民党

e.en: The {Janata} Party held a rally in Delhi yesterday.
e.zh: 人民党昨天在德里举行了集会。

e.en: Local news covered the {Janata} movement's recent reforms.
e.zh: 当地新闻报道了人民运动最近的改革。

e.en: {Jane} sent me a message about the meeting.
e.zh: 简给我发了一条关于会议的消息。

e.en: The novel's heroine {Jane} grows up in poverty.
e.zh: 小说的女主角简在贫困中长大。

janeiro.t: n. 一月（葡语，多见于 Rio de Janeiro）

e.en: We spent a week in Rio de {Janeiro} last summer.
e.zh: 我们去年夏天在里约热内卢待了一周。

e.en: Carnival in Rio de {Janeiro} attracts millions of tourists.
e.zh: 里约热内卢的狂欢节吸引了数百万游客。

jangle.t:
v. 发出刺耳叮当声
n. 刺耳金属声

e.en: The keys {jangle} in his pocket as he walks.
e.zh: 他走路时口袋里的钥匙叮当作响。

e.en: Loud noises {jangle} my nerves after a long day.
e.zh: 一天工作后,嘈杂的声音让我心烦意乱。

jangled.t:
v. jangle 的过去式
adj. 烦乱的

e.en: The bells {jangled} loudly when the door opened.
e.zh: 门一打开,铃铛就叮当作响。

e.en: Her nerves were {jangled} after the stressful interview.
e.zh: 紧张的面试后,她的神经一直紧绷着。

e.en: I heard the {jangling} of coins in his pocket.
e.zh: 我听到他口袋里硬币叮当作响。

e.en: The {jangling} alarm finally woke everyone up.
e.zh: 刺耳的闹钟铃声终于把大家都吵醒了。

jangly.t: adj. 发出叮当声的；刺耳的

e.en: The band has a {jangly} guitar sound from the eighties.
e.zh: 这支乐队有着八十年代叮当作响的吉他音色。

e.en: She wore {jangly} bracelets that made noise with every move.
e.zh: 她戴着一动就叮当响的手镯。

janitor.t: n. 看门人；楼管；清洁工

e.en: The {janitor} mops the hallway every night after class.
e.zh: 门卫每晚下课后都会拖走廊。

e.en: Our school {janitor} knows every student by name.
e.zh: 我们学校的清洁工记得每个学生的名字。

janitorial.t: adj. 门卫的；清洁工作的

e.en: The company hired a {janitorial} service to clean the offices.
e.zh: 公司雇了一家清洁公司来打扫办公室。

e.en: He started his career doing {janitorial} work at night.
e.zh: 他职业生涯始于晚上做清洁工作。

e.en: Recent {Januaries} have been unusually warm in our region.
e.zh: 近几年的一月在我们这里出奇地暖和。

e.en: She remembered the cold {Januaries} of her childhood fondly.
e.zh: 她深情地回忆起童年时寒冷的一月。

e.en: The new semester always begins in early {January}.
e.zh: 新学期总是在一月初开始。

e.en: {January} is usually the coldest month of the year.
e.zh: 一月通常是一年中最冷的月份。

janus.t: n. 雅努斯（罗马双面神）

e.en: The {Janus}-faced policy confused both supporters and critics.
e.zh: 这项两面性的政策让支持者和批评者都感到困惑。

e.en: Romans named the month after the god {Janus}.
e.zh: 罗马人以神雅努斯的名字命名这个月份。

jap.t: n. 日本人（蔑称，冒犯语）

e.en: The slur {jap} is offensive and should never be used.
e.zh: "jap"这个词带有侮辱性,绝不应使用。

e.en: Old wartime posters often included the racist term {jap}.
e.zh: 旧的战时海报上经常有带种族歧视的"jap"一词。

japan.t:
n. 日本
n. 日本漆器

e.en: I'm flying to {Japan} next month for vacation.
e.zh: 我下个月要飞去日本度假。

e.en: {Japan} is famous for its high-speed bullet trains.
e.zh: 日本以高速新干线列车闻名。

japanese.t:
adj. 日本的
n. 日本人；日语

e.en: She's learning {Japanese} to watch anime without subtitles.
e.zh: 她在学日语,这样看动漫就不用字幕了。

e.en: The {Japanese} restaurant downtown has the best sushi.
e.zh: 市中心那家日本餐厅的寿司是最好的。

jape.t:
n. 玩笑
v. 开玩笑

e.en: His silly {jape} made the whole class laugh.
e.zh: 他愚蠢的玩笑逗得全班哈哈大笑。

e.en: The comedian opened the show with a clever {jape}.
e.zh: 喜剧演员用一个巧妙的笑话开场。

e.en: The {japonica} bush in our garden bloomed bright red.
e.zh: 我们花园里的日本贴梗海棠开出了鲜红的花。

e.en: She planted a {japonica} near the front porch.
e.zh: 她在前廊附近种了一棵山茶花。

jar.t:
n. 广口瓶；罐子
v. 震动；不协调

e.en: Please pass me the {jar} of peanut butter.
e.zh: 请把那罐花生酱递给我。

e.en: Loud sounds always {jar} me out of deep sleep.
e.zh: 巨响总是把我从沉睡中惊醒。

jardin.t: n. 花园（法语/西语借词）

e.en: We strolled through the famous {Jardin} des Tuileries in Paris.
e.zh: 我们在巴黎著名的杜乐丽花园里漫步。

e.en: The hotel overlooks a beautiful {jardin} full of roses.
e.zh: 酒店俯瞰一座种满玫瑰的美丽花园。

e.en: The lawyer used legal {jargon} I couldn't understand.
e.zh: 那位律师用了我听不懂的法律行话。

e.en: Tech companies are full of meaningless corporate {jargon}.
e.zh: 科技公司里满是毫无意义的企业行话。

e.en: Different industries develop their own technical {jargons} over time.
e.zh: 不同行业会随着时间形成各自的专业术语。

e.en: Medical and legal {jargons} often confuse ordinary readers.
e.zh: 医学和法律术语常常让普通读者感到困惑。

jarhead.t: n. 美国海军陆战队员（俚语）

e.en: He proudly called himself a {jarhead} after joining the Marines.
e.zh: 加入海军陆战队后,他自豪地称自己为陆战队员。

e.en: The film depicts the harsh life of a young {jarhead}.
e.zh: 这部电影描绘了一名年轻陆战队员的艰苦生活。

jarred.t: v. 使震动；不协调（过去式）

e.en: The sudden noise {jarred} her awake at midnight.
e.zh: 突然的噪音在午夜把她惊醒。

e.en: His rude comment {jarred} the otherwise pleasant conversation.
e.zh: 他粗鲁的话破坏了原本愉快的谈话。

e.en: The transition between scenes felt {jarring} and confusing.
e.zh: 场景之间的切换显得突兀又令人困惑。

e.en: Her bright outfit was {jarring} against the gray background.
e.zh: 她鲜艳的衣着在灰色背景下显得格外刺眼。

e.en: The music ended {jarringly} in the middle of the chorus.
e.zh: 音乐在副歌中段戛然而止,十分突兀。

e.en: His tone changed {jarringly} from friendly to hostile.
e.zh: 他的语气突兀地从友好变得充满敌意。

e.en: The {Jarrow} March of 1936 protested mass unemployment in England.
e.zh: 1936年的贾罗游行抗议了英国大规模失业。

e.en: My grandfather grew up in {Jarrow} during the war.
e.zh: 我祖父在战争期间成长于贾罗。

jars.t:
n. 罐子（复数）
v. 震动

e.en: She filled several {jars} with homemade strawberry jam.
e.zh: 她装了好几罐自制的草莓酱。

e.en: The constant beeping {jars} my concentration at work.
e.zh: 持续的哔哔声打扰了我工作时的专注。

jeddah.t: n. 吉达（沙特阿拉伯城市）

e.en: The flight from Dubai to {Jeddah} takes three hours.
e.zh: 从迪拜飞往吉达的航班需要三个小时。

e.en: She moved to {Jeddah} for a teaching job last year.
e.zh: 她去年因一份教职搬到了吉达。

e.en: They drove a rented {jeep} across the desert.
e.zh: 他们开着租来的吉普车穿越沙漠。

e.en: The old {jeep} handled the muddy trail without trouble.
e.zh: 那辆旧吉普车在泥泞的小路上毫无障碍。

jeer.t:
v. 嘲笑；讥讽
n. 嘲弄

e.en: The crowd began to {jeer} at the losing team.
e.zh: 观众开始嘲讽那支输球的队伍。

e.en: Don't {jeer} when someone makes an honest mistake.
e.zh: 别人无心犯错时,别去嘲笑他。

jeering.t:
adj. 嘲讽的
n. 嘲笑声

e.en: The {jeering} fans made the player lose focus.
e.zh: 那些起哄的球迷让球员失去了专注。

e.en: She ignored the {jeering} comments on her video.
e.zh: 她对视频下的嘲讽留言视而不见。

jeeves.t: n. 吉夫斯（人名，常指贴身男仆）

e.en: He runs his household like a real-life {Jeeves}.
e.zh: 他像现实版的吉夫斯一样打理家务。

e.en: Wodehouse's {Jeeves} solves every problem with quiet wit.
e.zh: 伍德豪斯笔下的吉夫斯总是用机智悄悄化解难题。

jeez.t: int. 天哪；我的天（表惊讶）

e.en: {Jeez}, that movie was way longer than expected.
e.zh: 天哪,那部电影比想象的长太多了。

e.en: {Jeez}, you scared me coming in so quietly!
e.zh: 天啊,你这么悄悄进来吓了我一跳!

jefe.t: n. 老板；头儿（西语借词）

e.en: The {jefe} called everyone in for an early meeting.
e.zh: 老板把大家叫去开早会。

e.en: Ask the {jefe} before approving any new expenses.
e.zh: 批新开支之前先问问老板。

jefferson.t: n. 杰斐逊（姓氏，美国总统）

e.en: {Jefferson} drafted much of the Declaration of Independence.
e.zh: 杰斐逊起草了《独立宣言》的大部分内容。

e.en: They visited {Jefferson}'s home at Monticello last summer.
e.zh: 他们去年夏天参观了杰斐逊在蒙蒂塞洛的故居。

e.en: He defended a {Jeffersonian} view of limited federal power.
e.zh: 他坚持杰斐逊式的有限联邦权力观点。

e.en: The essay critiques {Jeffersonian} ideals about rural democracy.
e.zh: 这篇文章批评了杰斐逊式的乡村民主理想。

e.en: The hymn praises {Jehovah} as a faithful protector.
e.zh: 这首赞美诗颂扬耶和华是忠实的护佑者。

e.en: Two {Jehovah}'s Witnesses knocked on the door this morning.
e.zh: 今早两位耶和华见证人敲了门。

e.en: The surgeon repaired a small {jejunal} tear during surgery.
e.zh: 外科医生在手术中修复了一处小的空肠撕裂。

e.en: A {jejunal} feeding tube was inserted for nutrition support.
e.zh: 为营养支持插入了一根空肠喂养管。

e.en: His arguments seemed {jejune} compared to the senior researchers'.
e.zh: 和资深研究员相比,他的论点显得肤浅幼稚。

e.en: The novel's plot is unfortunately {jejune} and predictable.
e.zh: 这部小说的情节遗憾地显得乏味又老套。

e.en: The {jejunum} absorbs most nutrients from digested food.
e.zh: 空肠吸收消化食物中的大部分营养。

e.en: Doctors examined the {jejunum} for signs of inflammation.
e.zh: 医生检查了空肠是否有炎症迹象。

jekyll.t: n. 杰基尔（《化身博士》人物）

e.en: He has a {Jekyll} and Hyde personality at work.
e.zh: 他在工作中有种化身博士般的双重人格。

e.en: My blog is built using {Jekyll} and hosted on GitHub.
e.zh: 我的博客用Jekyll搭建,托管在GitHub上。

jell.t: v. 凝结；成形；（想法）变清晰

e.en: Give the team time to {jell} before judging performance.
e.zh: 评判表现之前,给团队一点磨合的时间。

e.en: The pudding will {jell} after an hour in the fridge.
e.zh: 布丁在冰箱里放一小时后就会凝固。

jellied.t: adj. 凝结成冻的；果冻状的

e.en: She served {jellied} cranberries with the holiday turkey.
e.zh: 她用蔓越莓冻搭配节日火鸡。

e.en: Traditional pubs still sell {jellied} eels in East London.
e.zh: 东伦敦的传统酒吧仍在卖鳗鱼冻。

e.en: The kids ate green {jello} after lunch.
e.zh: 孩子们午饭后吃了绿色的果冻。

e.en: My legs felt like {jello} after the long hike.
e.zh: 长途徒步后我的腿软得像果冻。

jelly.t:
n. 果冻；果酱
v. 使凝结

e.en: He spread strawberry {jelly} on his morning toast.
e.zh: 他在早餐吐司上抹了草莓果酱。

e.en: A clear {jelly} fish drifted near the shore.
e.zh: 一只透明的水母在岸边漂浮。

e.en: A glowing {jellyfish} drifted past the diver's mask.
e.zh: 一只发光的水母从潜水员面罩前漂过。

e.en: Don't touch that {jellyfish} — its sting really hurts.
e.zh: 别碰那只水母,它蜇人非常疼。

e.en: Grandma baked a strawberry {jellyroll} for the picnic.
e.zh: 奶奶为野餐烤了一个草莓果酱蛋糕卷。

e.en: He sliced the {jellyroll} into thick spirals for dessert.
e.zh: 他把果酱蛋糕卷切成厚厚的螺旋状作为甜点。

jemmy.t:
n. 撬棍
v. 撬开

e.en: The burglar used a {jemmy} to pry open the window.
e.zh: 窃贼用撬棍撬开了窗户。

e.en: Police found a {jemmy} hidden under the back seat.
e.zh: 警察在后座下发现了一根撬棍。

e.en: She studied physics at the University of {Jena}.
e.zh: 她在耶拿大学学习物理。

e.en: Napoleon defeated the Prussians near {Jena} in 1806.
e.zh: 拿破仑1806年在耶拿附近击败了普鲁士军队。

e.en: A stubborn {jenny} refused to cross the narrow bridge.
e.zh: 一头倔强的母驴不肯过那座窄桥。

e.en: The spinning {jenny} transformed the textile industry forever.
e.zh: 珍妮纺纱机彻底改变了纺织业。

jeopardise.t: v. 危及；使处于险境（英式拼法）

e.en: One careless tweet could {jeopardise} the entire deal.
e.zh: 一条不经意的推文可能让整笔交易陷入危险。

e.en: Don't {jeopardise} your health by skipping meals.
e.zh: 别因不吃饭而拿自己的健康冒险。

jeopardised.t:
v. jeopardise 的过去式
adj. 受到危及的

e.en: The leak {jeopardised} months of careful negotiation.
e.zh: 泄密事件让数月的谨慎谈判付诸东流。

e.en: Her absence {jeopardised} the team's chances of winning.
e.zh: 她的缺席让球队获胜的机会变得渺茫。

jeopardises.t: v. jeopardise 的第三人称单数

e.en: Skipping security updates {jeopardises} every user's data.
e.zh: 跳过安全更新会危及每位用户的数据。

e.en: His reckless driving {jeopardises} the safety of passengers.
e.zh: 他鲁莽的开车方式威胁着乘客的安全。

e.en: She kept quiet to avoid {jeopardising} her promotion.
e.zh: 她保持沉默,以免影响自己的升职。

e.en: They worried that protests were {jeopardising} the peace talks.
e.zh: 他们担心抗议活动正在危及和平谈判。

e.en: In Iron Man, {Jarvis} is Tony Stark's AI assistant.
e.zh: 在《钢铁侠》里,贾维斯是托尼·斯塔克的AI助手。

e.en: My friend {Jarvis} works as a software engineer downtown.
e.zh: 我朋友贾维斯在市中心做软件工程师。

e.en: My nickname {Jas} is short for Jasmine.
e.zh: 我的昵称Jas是茉莉的简称。

e.en: {Jas} sent me a quick text about the party.
e.zh: 小贾给我发了条关于聚会的简讯。

jasmine.t:
n. 茉莉花
n. 茉莉（女子名）

e.en: The garden smells of {jasmine} every spring evening.
e.zh: 每个春天的傍晚,花园里都弥漫着茉莉花香。

e.en: I love drinking {jasmine} tea after dinner.
e.zh: 我喜欢晚饭后喝茉莉花茶。

e.en: {Jason} just got promoted to senior manager last week.
e.zh: 杰森上周刚升任高级经理。

e.en: In Greek myth, {Jason} sailed to find the Golden Fleece.
e.zh: 在希腊神话中,伊阿宋航海寻找金羊毛。

jasper.t:
n. 碧玉（宝石）
n. 贾斯帕（人名）

e.en: She wore a beautiful necklace made of red {jasper}.
e.zh: 她戴着一条用红碧玉做的漂亮项链。

e.en: My cousin {Jasper} loves collecting unusual rocks and minerals.
e.zh: 我表弟贾斯珀喜欢收藏稀奇的石头和矿物。

jaundice.t:
n. 黄疸
n. 偏见、成见

e.en: The newborn developed mild {jaundice} a few days after birth.
e.zh: 新生儿出生几天后出现了轻微的黄疸。

e.en: Yellow eyes can be a sign of {jaundice}.
e.zh: 眼白发黄可能是黄疸的征兆。

jaundiced.t:
adj. 有偏见的、消极的
adj. 患黄疸的

e.en: He took a {jaundiced} view of the company's promises.
e.zh: 他对公司的承诺持怀疑和偏见的态度。

e.en: The patient looked pale and {jaundiced} after the illness.
e.zh: 病人在生病后看起来面色苍白且发黄。

jaunt.t:
n. 短途旅行
v. 作短途旅行

e.en: We took a quick {jaunt} to the coast last weekend.
e.zh: 上周末我们快速去海边玩了一趟。

e.en: A weekend {jaunt} to Paris sounds wonderful right now.
e.zh: 现在去巴黎来个周末小旅行听起来真棒。

jauntily.t: adv. 轻快地、得意洋洋地

e.en: He walked {jauntily} down the street whistling a tune.
e.zh: 他吹着小调,神气活现地走在街上。

e.en: She wore her hat {jauntily} tilted to one side.
e.zh: 她俏皮地把帽子歪向一边戴着。

jaunty.t: adj. 轻快的、活泼自信的

e.en: He gave a {jaunty} wave as he left the room.
e.zh: 他离开房间时神气地挥了挥手。

e.en: The song has a {jaunty} rhythm that makes you smile.
e.zh: 这首歌有种轻快的节奏,让人忍不住微笑。

java.t:
n. Java 编程语言
n. 爪哇岛；咖啡（俚语）

e.en: Most enterprise apps are still written in {Java}.
e.zh: 大多数企业应用程序仍然用Java编写。

e.en: I need a fresh cup of {java} to start my morning.
e.zh: 我需要一杯新煮的咖啡来开始我的早晨。

javan.t:
adj. 爪哇岛的
n. 爪哇人

e.en: The {Javan} rhino is one of the rarest mammals on Earth.
e.zh: 爪哇犀牛是地球上最稀有的哺乳动物之一。

e.en: {Javan} culture has deeply influenced Indonesian art and music.
e.zh: 爪哇文化深深影响了印尼的艺术和音乐。

javanese.t:
n. 爪哇人；爪哇语
adj. 爪哇的

e.en: She studied {Javanese} dance during her year in Indonesia.
e.zh: 她在印尼的那一年学习了爪哇舞蹈。

e.en: The {Javanese} language has multiple levels of formality.
e.zh: 爪哇语有多种不同的礼貌语级。

e.en: He threw the {javelin} farther than anyone else in the meet.
e.zh: 他在比赛中投掷标枪比其他任何人都远。

e.en: The athlete trained for years to master the {javelin}.
e.zh: 这位运动员训练多年才掌握标枪技术。

e.en: A {javelina} wandered through our backyard last night.
e.zh: 昨晚一只西貒在我们后院里游荡。

e.en: Hikers in Arizona sometimes encounter a wild {javelina}.
e.zh: 在亚利桑那州徒步时,有时会遇到野生西貒。

jaw.t:
n. 颌、下巴
v. 唠叨、闲谈

e.en: His {jaw} dropped when he heard the surprising news.
e.zh: 听到这令人惊讶的消息时,他下巴都掉下来了。

e.en: She injured her {jaw} during the boxing match.
e.zh: 她在拳击比赛中伤到了下巴。

jawbone.t:
n. 颌骨
v. 劝说、施压

e.en: The fossil's {jawbone} helped scientists identify the species.
e.zh: 这块化石的颌骨帮助科学家鉴定出物种。

e.en: He broke his {jawbone} in a skateboarding accident.
e.zh: 他在滑板事故中摔断了下颌骨。

jawbreaker.t:
n. 硬糖球
n. 拗口的词

e.en: That candy is a real {jawbreaker} — be careful.
e.zh: 那颗糖真是块巨型硬糖,小心咬。

e.en: The kids spent their allowance on a giant {jawbreaker}.
e.zh: 孩子们用零花钱买了一颗巨大的硬糖球。

e.en: The model is famous for her sharp {jawline}.
e.zh: 这位模特以她轮廓分明的下颌线而闻名。

e.en: He grew a beard to soften his angular {jawline}.
e.zh: 他留了胡子来柔化他棱角分明的下颌线。

jaws.t:
n. 颌（jaw 的复数）
n. 电影《大白鲨》

e.en: The crocodile's powerful {jaws} can crush bones easily.
e.zh: 鳄鱼有力的颚部能轻易咬碎骨头。

e.en: The classic film {Jaws} still terrifies viewers today.
e.zh: 经典电影《大白鲨》至今仍让观众心惊胆战。

jay.t:
n. 松鸦（鸟类）
n. 杰伊（人名）

e.en: A blue {jay} landed on the bird feeder this morning.
e.zh: 今天早上一只蓝松鸦落在了喂鸟器上。

e.en: My cousin {Jay} is moving to Seattle next month.
e.zh: 我表弟杰下个月要搬去西雅图。

jaya.t: n. 贾娅（人名，源自梵语"胜利"）

e.en: She named her daughter {Jaya}, meaning victory in Sanskrit.
e.zh: 她给女儿取名Jaya,在梵语中意为胜利。

e.en: Puncak {Jaya} is the highest peak in Indonesia.
e.zh: 查亚峰是印度尼西亚的最高峰。

e.en: A noisy {jaybird} landed on the fence this morning.
e.zh: 今早一只吵闹的松鸦落在了篱笆上。

e.en: He stood there naked as a {jaybird} after the prank.
e.zh: 被恶作剧后他光溜溜地站在那里。

jaywalk.t: v. 不守规则横穿马路

e.en: Don't {jaywalk} across this busy intersection.
e.zh: 不要在这个繁忙的路口乱穿马路。

e.en: Tourists often {jaywalk} without realizing it's illegal here.
e.zh: 游客常常乱穿马路,却不知道这里是违法的。

e.en: The officer fined a {jaywalker} crossing against the red light.
e.zh: 警察对一名闯红灯横穿马路的行人开了罚单。

e.en: Drivers in this city watch out for every {jaywalker}.
e.zh: 这座城市的司机会留意每一个乱穿马路的人。

jazz.t:
n. 爵士乐
v. 使活泼、装饰

e.en: She listens to {jazz} while cooking dinner.
e.zh: 她做晚饭时会听爵士乐。

e.en: Skip the {jazz} and tell me what really happened.
e.zh: 别绕弯子,告诉我究竟发生了什么。

jazzed.t:
adj. 兴奋激动的
adj. 装饰花哨的

e.en: I'm really {jazzed} about the new project launch.
e.zh: 我对新项目的发布感到非常兴奋。

e.en: They {jazzed} up the homepage with brighter colors.
e.zh: 他们用更鲜艳的色彩让主页变得有活力。

e.en: The old {jazzman} played trumpet at the corner club.
e.zh: 那位老爵士乐手在街角酒吧吹小号。

e.en: Every {jazzman} in town came to the late-night jam.
e.zh: 城里的每位爵士乐手都来到了深夜即兴演奏会。

jazzs.t: n. jazz 的非标准复数形式

e.en: She {jazzs} up plain salads with toasted nuts.
e.zh: 她用烤坚果让普通沙拉变得有滋味。

e.en: That café {jazzs} its menu every season.
e.zh: 那家咖啡馆每个季节都会让菜单焕然一新。

jazzy.t:
adj. 花哨抢眼的
adj. 爵士风格的

e.en: He wore a {jazzy} tie to the office party.
e.zh: 他戴着一条花哨的领带去公司派对。

e.en: The app got a {jazzy} new interface this week.
e.zh: 这款应用本周换上了一个时髦的新界面。

jcb.t: n. JCB（英国工程机械品牌）

e.en: A yellow {jcb} dug the foundation for the new house.
e.zh: 一台黄色挖掘机为新房挖了地基。

e.en: The construction site has three {jcb} machines working today.
e.zh: 工地今天有三台JCB挖掘机在作业。

jealous.t:
adj. 嫉妒的、吃醋的
adj. 戒备的、珍视的

e.en: She felt {jealous} when her friend got the promotion.
e.zh: 朋友升职时她心里有些嫉妒。

e.en: I'm {jealous} of your trip to Japan next month.
e.zh: 我真羡慕你下个月要去日本旅行。

jealously.t: adv. 嫉妒地；小心守护地

e.en: He {jealously} guarded his passwords from coworkers.
e.zh: 他小心翼翼地不让同事看到他的密码。

e.en: She watched the new intern {jealously} from her desk.
e.zh: 她坐在桌前嫉妒地盯着那个新实习生。

e.en: His {jealousy} eventually destroyed their friendship.
e.zh: 他的嫉妒最终毁掉了他们的友谊。

e.en: A flash of {jealousy} crossed her face during the meeting.
e.zh: 会议中她脸上闪过一丝嫉妒。

jean.t:
n. 斜纹粗棉布
n. 简（人名）

e.en: She bought a {jean} jacket for the autumn weather.
e.zh: 她买了件牛仔夹克来应对秋天的天气。

e.en: He prefers {jean} fabric for casual everyday wear.
e.zh: 他喜欢用牛仔布料做日常便装。

e.en: I wear {jeans} to the office on Fridays.
e.zh: 周五我会穿牛仔裤去上班。

e.en: These {jeans} fit better after a few washes.
e.zh: 这条牛仔裤洗几次后更合身了。

e.en: Don't {jeopardize} your career over a silly argument.
e.zh: 别为一场无聊的争吵毁了自己的事业。

e.en: Bad weather could {jeopardize} the launch tomorrow.
e.zh: 恶劣天气可能会让明天的发射告吹。

jeopardized.t: v. 危及（jeopardize 的过去式）

e.en: The scandal {jeopardized} her chances of reelection.
e.zh: 这场丑闻危及了她连任的可能。

e.en: A single bug {jeopardized} the whole product release.
e.zh: 一个小bug危及了整个产品发布。

jeopardizes.t: v. 危及（jeopardize 的第三人称单数）

e.en: Sharing passwords {jeopardizes} the entire company's network.
e.zh: 共享密码会危及整个公司的网络安全。

e.en: Constant overtime {jeopardizes} both health and productivity.
e.zh: 长期加班既损害健康也影响效率。

jeopardizing.t: v. 危及（jeopardize 的现在分词）

e.en: He's {jeopardizing} his marriage by working every weekend.
e.zh: 他每个周末加班,正在让自己的婚姻陷入危机。

e.en: The startup avoided {jeopardizing} user trust during the outage.
e.zh: 那家创业公司在故障期间避免了损害用户信任。

e.en: The merger put hundreds of jobs in {jeopardy}.
e.zh: 这次合并让数百个工作岗位陷入危险。

e.en: Her reputation was in serious {jeopardy} after the leak.
e.zh: 泄密之后,她的名誉岌岌可危。

e.en: His column read like a long {jeremiad} about modern life.
e.zh: 他的专栏读起来像是对现代生活的长篇控诉。

e.en: She delivered a {jeremiad} against social media at dinner.
e.zh: 晚餐时她对社交媒体发表了一通控诉。

jeremiah.t: n. 耶利米（圣经先知/人名）

e.en: The prophet {Jeremiah} warned of impending disaster.
e.zh: 先知耶利米警告灾难即将来临。

e.en: He sounded like a modern {Jeremiah} predicting economic doom.
e.zh: 他像现代版耶利米一样预言经济崩溃。

e.en: Tourists visit {Jericho} to see one of Earth's oldest cities.
e.zh: 游客们到耶利哥参观这座地球上最古老的城市之一。

e.en: The walls of {Jericho} fell, according to the biblical story.
e.zh: 据《圣经》记载,耶利哥的城墙倒塌了。

jerk.t:
n. 蠢货；混蛋
v. 猛地一动

e.en: Don't be a {jerk} to the new intern.
e.zh: 别对新来的实习生那么混蛋。

e.en: The car stopped with a sudden {jerk} at the light.
e.zh: 车在红灯前猛地一颠停了下来。

e.en: The old projector advanced the film {jerkily} frame by frame.
e.zh: 旧放映机一帧一帧地抖动着推进胶片。

e.en: He danced {jerkily}, completely out of rhythm with the music.
e.zh: 他动作生硬地跳着舞，完全跟不上节奏。

jerkin.t: n. (旧时) 男式紧身背心

e.en: The actor wore a leather {jerkin} for the medieval scene.
e.zh: 演员在中世纪场景中穿着一件皮制紧身上衣。

e.en: Robin Hood is often pictured in a green {jerkin}.
e.zh: 罗宾汉常被描绘成穿着绿色紧身上衣的形象。

jerking.t: v. 猛拉；抽动（jerk 的现在分词）

e.en: Stop {jerking} the steering wheel so hard around corners.
e.zh: 过弯时别那么猛地拉方向盘。

e.en: His leg kept {jerking} involuntarily during the long flight.
e.zh: 长途飞行中他的腿不由自主地一直抽动。

jerky.t:
n. 肉干
adj. 颠簸的

e.en: I packed beef {jerky} as a snack for the hike.
e.zh: 我带了牛肉干作为徒步时的零食。

e.en: The video playback was {jerky} due to a slow connection.
e.zh: 由于网络太慢，视频播放卡顿不流畅。

e.en: The shed was a {jerry}-built structure that collapsed in the storm.
e.zh: 那间棚屋偷工减料，在暴风雨中倒塌了。

e.en: My friend {Jerry} just opened a bakery downtown.
e.zh: 我朋友杰瑞刚在市中心开了一家面包店。

e.en: He bought a signed Lakers {jersey} at the auction.
e.zh: 他在拍卖会上买了一件有签名的湖人队球衣。

e.en: This sweater is made of soft cotton {jersey}.
e.zh: 这件毛衣由柔软的棉质平针织物制成。

e.en: The team unveiled their new home {jerseys} before the season.
e.zh: 球队在赛季开始前公布了新的主场球衣。

e.en: Fans lined up to buy {jerseys} of their favorite players.
e.zh: 球迷们排队购买自己喜爱球员的球衣。

e.en: {Jerusalem} is considered a holy city by three major religions.
e.zh: 耶路撒冷被三大宗教视为圣城。

e.en: We spent a week exploring the old city of {Jerusalem}.
e.zh: 我们花了一周时间游览耶路撒冷老城。

e.en: The garden was filled with the sweet scent of {jessamine}.
e.zh: 花园里弥漫着茉莉花的甜香。

e.en: Yellow {jessamine} climbs the trellis beside the porch.
e.zh: 黄色素馨花攀爬在门廊旁的格架上。

jest.t:
n. 玩笑；戏言
v. 开玩笑

e.en: He said it in {jest}, but she took it seriously.
e.zh: 他只是开玩笑说的，但她当真了。

e.en: Don't {jest} about such a sensitive topic at dinner.
e.zh: 晚餐时不要拿这么敏感的话题开玩笑。

jester.t: n. 弄臣；爱开玩笑的人

e.en: The court {jester} entertained the king with witty jokes.
e.zh: 宫廷小丑用机智的笑话逗国王开心。

e.en: He plays the office {jester}, always lightening the mood.
e.zh: 他在办公室里像个开心果，总能活跃气氛。

jesting.t: v. 开玩笑（jest 的现在分词）

e.en: Stop {jesting} and tell me what really happened last night.
e.zh: 别开玩笑了，告诉我昨晚到底发生了什么。

e.en: Her {jesting} tone hid a serious concern about the project.
e.zh: 她调侃的语气掩盖了对项目的真切担忧。

jesu.t: n. 耶稣（Jesus 的旧式称呼）

e.en: Bach's "{Jesu}, Joy of Man's Desiring" is played at many weddings.
e.zh: 巴赫的《耶稣，世人仰望的喜悦》常在婚礼上演奏。

e.en: The choir sang an old hymn beginning with "{Jesu}, lover of my soul."
e.zh: 唱诗班唱起以"耶稣，我灵之爱"开头的古老圣诗。

jesuit.t: n. 耶稣会士；耶稣会成员

e.en: The university was founded by {Jesuit} priests in the 1800s.
e.zh: 这所大学由耶稣会神父在十九世纪创办。

e.en: He received a rigorous {Jesuit} education in Boston.
e.zh: 他在波士顿接受了严格的耶稣会教育。

e.en: Christians believe that {Jesus} rose from the dead on Easter.
e.zh: 基督徒相信耶稣在复活节从死里复活。

e.en: "{Jesus}, that startled me!" she gasped, dropping the cup.
e.zh: "天哪，吓死我了！"她倒吸一口气，把杯子摔了。

jet.t:
n. 喷气式飞机；喷射
v. 喷射

e.en: A private {jet} landed at the small regional airport.
e.zh: 一架私人喷气机降落在那个小型支线机场。

e.en: A powerful {jet} of water shot from the broken pipe.
e.zh: 一股强劲的水柱从破裂的管道中喷出。

e.en: The new {jetliner} can carry over 400 passengers across oceans.
e.zh: 这款新型喷气客机可以载运超过400名乘客跨越海洋。

e.en: Boeing unveiled its latest fuel-efficient {jetliner} at the air show.
e.zh: 波音在航展上发布了最新的节能喷气客机。

jets.t: n. 喷气机（jet 的复数）

e.en: Two fighter {jets} streaked across the morning sky.
e.zh: 两架战斗机划过清晨的天空。

e.en: The fountain {jets} water fifteen meters into the air.
e.zh: 喷泉将水柱喷射到十五米高的空中。

jetsam.t: n. 船舶抛入海中的货物

e.en: Beachcombers found bottles and other {jetsam} along the shore.
e.zh: 拾荒者在岸边发现了瓶子和其他被抛弃的漂浮物。

e.en: The old warehouse was full of the {jetsam} of past lives.
e.zh: 那座旧仓库里满是过往生活遗留的杂物。

e.en: The pilot had to {jettison} fuel before the emergency landing.
e.zh: 飞行员不得不在紧急降落前抛掉燃油。

e.en: The company decided to {jettison} its unprofitable mobile division.
e.zh: 公司决定砍掉亏损的移动业务部门。

e.en: We watched the sunset from the end of the wooden {jetty}.
e.zh: 我们在木栈桥的尽头观看日落。

e.en: Fishermen tied their boats along the stone {jetty}.
e.zh: 渔民们把船拴在石砌的防波堤旁。

e.en: Passengers walked down the {jetway} and boarded the plane.
e.zh: 乘客们走过登机廊桥，登上了飞机。

e.en: A mechanical issue with the {jetway} delayed our boarding by an hour.
e.zh: 登机桥的机械故障让我们的登机推迟了一小时。

e.en: The boutique markets itself to {jeune} fashionable Parisians.
e.zh: 这家精品店主打巴黎年轻时尚人群。

e.en: The novel captures the spirit of the {jeune} generation in Paris.
e.zh: 这部小说捕捉了巴黎年轻一代的精神。

e.en: The film celebrates the wild {jeunesse} of 1960s Paris.
e.zh: 这部电影歌颂了1960年代巴黎狂野的青春岁月。

e.en: "{Jeunesse} dorée" refers to wealthy, fashionable young people.
e.zh: "镀金青年"一词指富有时髦的年轻人。

jeux.t: n. 游戏（法语，jeu 的复数）

e.en: Debussy composed a ballet titled "{Jeux}" in 1913.
e.zh: 德彪西在1913年创作了名为《游戏》的芭蕾舞剧。

e.en: The phrase "{jeux} d'esprit" means clever, playful witticisms.
e.zh: "jeux d'esprit"一词意为机智俏皮的妙语。

e.en: As a {Jew}, he observes the Sabbath every Friday evening.
e.zh: 作为一名犹太人，他每周五晚都守安息日。

e.en: The synagogue welcomes any {Jew} seeking community.
e.zh: 这座犹太教堂欢迎任何寻求归属的犹太人。

e.en: The crown's central {jewel} sparkled under the museum lights.
e.zh: 王冠中央的宝石在博物馆灯光下闪闪发光。

e.en: This little café is a real {jewel} of the neighborhood.
e.zh: 这家小咖啡馆是社区里真正的瑰宝。

e.en: She wore a {jeweled} hairpin at the formal gala.
e.zh: 她在正式晚会上戴了一支镶宝石的发簪。

e.en: The antique dagger had a {jeweled} handle worth a fortune.
e.zh: 那把古董匕首的手柄镶满宝石，价值连城。

e.en: The {jeweler} resized my grandmother's ring perfectly.
e.zh: 珠宝匠完美地调整了我奶奶戒指的尺寸。

e.en: She visited a local {jeweler} to design her engagement ring.
e.zh: 她去了当地一家珠宝店定制订婚戒指。

e.en: Several {jewelers} offered estimates for the antique necklace.
e.zh: 几家珠宝商对那条古董项链给出了估价。

e.en: Fifth Avenue is famous for its luxury {jewelers}.
e.zh: 第五大道以其奢华的珠宝商店而闻名。

jewelled.t: adj. 镶有宝石的（英式拼写）

e.en: The queen's crown was {jewelled} with rubies and emeralds.
e.zh: 女王的王冠镶嵌着红宝石和绿宝石。

e.en: He gave her a delicate {jewelled} brooch as a gift.
e.zh: 他送给她一枚精致的宝石胸针作为礼物。

e.en: The {jeweller} on High Street offers free ring cleaning.
e.zh: 高街上那家珠宝店提供免费洗戒指服务。

e.en: My uncle worked as a {jeweller} for over forty years.
e.zh: 我叔叔做珠宝匠做了四十多年。

jewelleries.t: n. 珠宝首饰（英式，复数）

e.en: Several heritage {jewelleries} in the old quarter still craft pieces by hand.
e.zh: 老城区里几家老字号珠宝店仍在手工打造首饰。

e.en: The mall houses both luxury {jewelleries} and budget accessory stores.
e.zh: 购物中心里既有奢华珠宝店，也有平价饰品店。

e.en: London's Hatton Garden is home to many famous {jewellers}.
e.zh: 伦敦的哈顿花园有许多著名珠宝商。

e.en: Two {jewellers} appraised the necklace at very different values.
e.zh: 两位珠宝商对这条项链给出了截然不同的估价。

jewellery.t: n. 珠宝首饰（英式拼写）

e.en: She keeps her grandmother's {jewellery} in a velvet box.
e.zh: 她把奶奶的首饰存放在一个天鹅绒盒子里。

e.en: The boutique sells handmade silver {jewellery} from local artisans.
e.zh: 这家精品店出售本地工匠手工制作的银饰。

e.en: Various {jewelries} from the dynasty are displayed at the museum.
e.zh: 博物馆展出了那个朝代的各种珠宝首饰。

e.en: She inherited several antique {jewelries} from her great-aunt.
e.zh: 她从姑婆那里继承了几件古董首饰。

e.en: She rarely wears expensive {jewelry} to work.
e.zh: 她很少戴贵重首饰上班。

e.en: The store specializes in handcrafted silver {jewelry}.
e.zh: 这家店专营手工银饰。

e.en: The royal {jewels} are kept in the Tower of London.
e.zh: 皇家珠宝收藏在伦敦塔内。

e.en: These vintage cafés are the hidden {jewels} of the city.
e.zh: 这些复古咖啡馆是这座城市的隐藏瑰宝。

e.en: Crushed {jewelweed} leaves can soothe poison ivy rashes.
e.zh: 捣碎的凤仙花叶可以缓解毒藤引起的皮疹。

e.en: Hummingbirds love the orange flowers of wild {jewelweed}.
e.zh: 蜂鸟很喜欢野生凤仙花的橙色花朵。

e.en: The novel's protagonist is a young {Jewess} living in 19th-century Vienna.
e.zh: 小说的主人公是一位生活在十九世纪维也纳的年轻犹太女子。

e.en: The term "{Jewess}" is now considered old-fashioned and is rarely used.
e.zh: "Jewess"一词如今被视为过时用法，已很少使用。

jewish.t: adj. 犹太人的；犹太教的

e.en: They observe many {Jewish} traditions during Hanukkah.
e.zh: 他们在光明节期间会遵循许多犹太传统。

e.en: The deli serves classic {Jewish} comfort food like matzo ball soup.
e.zh: 这家熟食店供应像无酵饼丸子汤这样的经典犹太家常美食。

jewishness.t: n. 犹太人身份或特质

e.en: The author explores her sense of {Jewishness} in the memoir.
e.zh: 作者在回忆录中探讨了自己的犹太身份认同。

e.en: His {Jewishness} shaped much of his cultural identity growing up.
e.zh: 犹太身份深深塑造了他成长过程中的文化认同。

e.en: The museum documents the history of European {Jewry} before the war.
e.zh: 博物馆记录了战前欧洲犹太民族的历史。

e.en: American {Jewry} has played a significant role in cultural life.
e.zh: 美国犹太族群在文化生活中扮演了重要角色。

jewson.t: n. 人名或英国建材连锁品牌

e.en: I picked up some timber from {Jewson} for the deck repair.
e.zh: 我去Jewson建材店买了些木材来修露台。

e.en: {Jewson} is one of the largest builders' merchants in Britain.
e.zh: Jewson是英国最大的建材供应商之一。

e.en: The tabloids painted her as a scheming {Jezebel}.
e.zh: 小报把她描绘成一个工于心计的荡妇。

e.en: In the Bible, Queen {Jezebel} is portrayed as deeply wicked.
e.zh: 在《圣经》中，耶洗别王后被描绘为极其邪恶的人。

jfk.t: n. 肯尼迪总统；纽约肯尼迪机场

e.en: My flight to Tokyo departs from {JFK} tomorrow morning.
e.zh: 我飞往东京的航班明早从肯尼迪机场起飞。

e.en: {JFK} was assassinated in Dallas on November 22, 1963.
e.zh: 肯尼迪总统于1963年11月22日在达拉斯遇刺身亡。

e.en: {Jiang} Zemin served as China's president throughout the 1990s.
e.zh: 江泽民在整个九十年代担任中国国家主席。

e.en: The Yangtze River is called Chang {Jiang} in Chinese.
e.zh: 长江在中文里被称为"长江"。

jib.t: n. 船首三角帆；起重机臂

e.en: The sailor adjusted the {jib} to catch the changing wind.
e.zh: 水手调整三角帆以借助变化的风向。

e.en: The crane's {jib} swung the steel beam into position.
e.zh: 起重机的吊臂把钢梁摆放到位。

jibe.t:
v. 相符一致
n. 嘲讽

e.en: His story doesn't quite {jibe} with what the witnesses said.
e.zh: 他的说法和目击者所说的不太吻合。

e.en: She brushed off his sarcastic {jibe} with a smile.
e.zh: 她微笑着对他讽刺的挖苦不以为意。

e.en: I added crunchy {jicama} sticks to the salad for texture.
e.zh: 我在沙拉里加了些脆爽的豆薯条增加口感。

e.en: {Jicama} tastes like a cross between an apple and a potato.
e.zh: 豆薯尝起来像苹果和土豆的混合体。

e.en: I'll be back in a {jiffy} with your coffee.
e.zh: 我马上就回来,给你拿咖啡。

e.en: The technician fixed the printer in a {jiffy}.
e.zh: 技术员一会儿就把打印机修好了。

jig.t:
n. 吉格舞
v. 上下晃动

e.en: He danced a little {jig} when he won the prize.
e.zh: 他得奖时高兴地跳了一段吉格舞。

e.en: The carpenter built a {jig} to cut identical pieces.
e.zh: 木工做了一个夹具来切出一样的零件。

e.en: Pour one {jigger} of rum into the cocktail shaker.
e.zh: 往调酒壶里倒一盎司朗姆酒。

e.en: The bartender measured gin with a steel {jigger}.
e.zh: 酒保用钢制量酒器量金酒。

e.en: The toddler kept {jigging} up and down with excitement.
e.zh: 小朋友兴奋得一直上下蹦跳。

e.en: Anglers were {jigging} for cod off the rocky coast.
e.zh: 渔民们在礁岸边用拟饵钓鳕鱼。

e.en: You have to {jiggle} the key to open this lock.
e.zh: 你得轻轻摇一下钥匙才能打开这把锁。

e.en: The jelly began to {jiggle} when she touched the plate.
e.zh: 她一碰盘子,果冻就晃了起来。

e.en: Stop {jiggling} the table while I'm trying to write.
e.zh: 我写字的时候你别一直晃桌子。

e.en: The phone kept {jiggling} on the desk from the vibrations.
e.zh: 手机震动得在桌上不停地颤。

e.en: We spent the rainy afternoon doing a 1000-piece {jigsaw}.
e.zh: 我们在雨天下午拼了一幅一千片的拼图。

e.en: He cut the curved shape with a {jigsaw}.
e.zh: 他用曲线锯切出弧形。

e.en: Scholars debate the true meaning of {jihad} in Islamic texts.
e.zh: 学者们争论伊斯兰经典中圣战的真正含义。

e.en: The mayor declared a personal {jihad} against street litter.
e.zh: 市长宣布要向街头垃圾发起一场个人圣战。

e.en: Authorities arrested a suspected {jihadi} at the border yesterday.
e.zh: 当局昨天在边境逮捕了一名圣战嫌疑分子。

e.en: The documentary traces how a {jihadi} network recruits online.
e.zh: 这部纪录片追踪一个圣战组织如何在网上招募成员。

e.en: The {jihadist} group claimed responsibility for the attack.
e.zh: 该圣战组织声称对这次袭击负责。

e.en: Analysts study {jihadist} propaganda spreading on social media.
e.zh: 分析人士研究在社交媒体上传播的圣战宣传。

e.en: There are a {jillion} reasons not to text your ex.
e.zh: 不该给前任发短信的理由多得数不清。

e.en: My inbox has a {jillion} unread emails this morning.
e.zh: 今天早上我收件箱里有无数封未读邮件。

e.en: She refused to {jilt} him just before the wedding.
e.zh: 她不愿在婚礼前抛弃他。

e.en: Don't {jilt} a loyal customer for a quick profit.
e.zh: 别为了一时利润抛弃忠实客户。

e.en: The {jilted} groom waited at the altar for an hour.
e.zh: 被抛弃的新郎在圣坛前等了一个小时。

e.en: Voters felt {jilted} after the politician broke his promises.
e.zh: 政客食言后,选民感到被抛弃了。

jimmies.t: n. 彩色糖粒（冰淇淋装饰）

e.en: The kids asked for rainbow {jimmies} on their ice cream.
e.zh: 孩子们要求在冰淇淋上撒彩虹巧克力米。

e.en: She sprinkled chocolate {jimmies} over the frosted cupcakes.
e.zh: 她在裹了糖霜的纸杯蛋糕上撒了巧克力米。

jimmy.t:
n. 撬棍
v. 用撬棍撬开

e.en: The burglar used a crowbar to {jimmy} the window open.
e.zh: 窃贼用撬棍把窗户撬开。

e.en: He had to {jimmy} the lock to get inside.
e.zh: 他不得不撬开锁才进得去。

jingle.t:
n. 叮当声；广告短曲
v. 发出叮当声

e.en: That catchy {jingle} from the ad is stuck in my head.
e.zh: 那段广告的洗脑小调一直在我脑子里转。

e.en: I heard the keys {jingle} as he walked up the stairs.
e.zh: 他上楼时,我听到钥匙叮当作响。

jingling.t: v. 叮当作响（jingle 的现在分词）

e.en: The bells were {jingling} softly above the shop door.
e.zh: 店门上方的铃铛轻轻地叮当响。

e.en: She walked away with coins {jingling} in her pocket.
e.zh: 她走开时口袋里的硬币叮当作响。

jingoism.t: n. 极端爱国主义；好战的沙文主义

e.en: The newspaper criticized the campaign's blatant {jingoism}.
e.zh: 该报批评了这场竞选中露骨的沙文主义。

e.en: Wartime {jingoism} often drowns out reasonable debate.
e.zh: 战时的极端爱国主义往往压过理性的讨论。

jingoistic.t: adj. 极端爱国的；好战沙文主义的

e.en: His {jingoistic} speech alarmed many foreign diplomats.
e.zh: 他那番沙文主义的演讲让许多外国外交官感到不安。

e.en: Critics called the film a {jingoistic} piece of propaganda.
e.zh: 批评者称这部电影是一部沙文主义的宣传片。

jink.t:
v. 急转躲避
n. 闪避动作

e.en: The fighter pilot had to {jink} to avoid the missile.
e.zh: 战斗机飞行员不得不急转弯以躲避导弹。

e.en: He saw the defender and tried to {jink} left.
e.zh: 他看到防守球员便试图向左急闪。

jinks.t: n. 嬉闹（常见于 high jinks 狂欢）

e.en: The students enjoyed some high {jinks} on graduation night.
e.zh: 毕业之夜,学生们尽情玩闹了一番。

e.en: Their summer was filled with harmless {jinks} and laughter.
e.zh: 他们的暑假里充满了无伤大雅的玩闹和笑声。

jinny.t: n. 小母驴；矿用小机车

e.en: The miners called their small locomotive a {jinny}.
e.zh: 矿工们把他们的小型机车叫做小马达车。

e.en: A patient {jinny} hauled coal carts up the slope.
e.zh: 一台耐用的小型卷扬机把煤车拉上斜坡。

jinx.t:
n. 不祥之物；霉运
v. 给…带来厄运

e.en: Don't say that — you'll {jinx} our chances of winning.
e.zh: 别这么说,你会让我们赢的机会泡汤的。

e.en: He thinks the green sweater is a total {jinx}.
e.zh: 他觉得那件绿毛衣完全是个不祥之物。

jitney.t: n. 廉价小型公共汽车

e.en: A small {jitney} shuttles tourists between the beach and town.
e.zh: 一辆小型公共车在海滩与镇上之间接送游客。

e.en: She caught the {jitney} to the airport for five dollars.
e.zh: 她花五美元坐小巴到机场。

jitter.t:
n. 抖动；信号抖动
v. 紧张不安

e.en: Network {jitter} can ruin a video call's audio quality.
e.zh: 网络抖动会毁掉视频通话的音质。

e.en: His hands began to {jitter} after three espressos.
e.zh: 喝了三杯浓缩咖啡后,他的手开始发抖。

jitterbug.t: n. 吉特巴舞（一种快节奏摇摆舞）

e.en: My grandparents loved to dance the {jitterbug} at parties.
e.zh: 我祖父母在派对上喜欢跳吉特巴舞。

e.en: She learned the {jitterbug} from an old swing instructor.
e.zh: 她跟一位老摇摆舞老师学了吉特巴。

jitters.t: n. 紧张不安；神经过敏

e.en: I always get the {jitters} before a job interview.
e.zh: 面试前我总是紧张得心慌。

e.en: Too much coffee gives me the {jitters} all afternoon.
e.zh: 咖啡喝多了我整个下午都心慌手抖。

jittery.t: adj. 紧张不安的；神经质的

e.en: Investors grew {jittery} after the surprise rate hike.
e.zh: 利率意外上调后,投资者变得紧张不安。

e.en: The puppy looked {jittery} during the thunderstorm.
e.zh: 雷暴中,那只小狗显得惊慌不安。

jive.t:
n. 摇摆舞；瞎扯
v. 跳摇摆舞

e.en: Her story doesn't {jive} with what the witnesses described.
e.zh: 她的说法与目击者描述的对不上。

e.en: They danced a fast {jive} at the wedding reception.
e.zh: 他们在婚宴上跳了一段快速的捷舞。

jna.t: abbr. 南斯拉夫人民军（Jugoslovenska Narodna Armija）

e.en: The historian wrote a chapter on the {JNA} during the breakup.
e.zh: 这位历史学家写了一章关于解体期间南斯拉夫人民军的内容。

e.en: Old uniforms of the {JNA} are now collector's items.
e.zh: 南斯拉夫人民军的旧军服现在成了收藏品。

jnr.t: abbr. 小（Junior 的缩写，用于人名后）

e.en: The letter was addressed to John Smith {Jnr}.
e.zh: 这封信是寄给小约翰·史密斯的。

e.en: Robert Downey {Jnr} starred in many superhero films.
e.zh: 小罗伯特·唐尼出演过许多超级英雄电影。

job.t:
n. 工作；职位；任务
v. 做零工

e.en: She just landed a new {job} at a tech startup.
e.zh: 她刚在一家科技创业公司找到了新工作。

e.en: Cleaning the gutters is a tedious {job}.
e.zh: 清理排水沟是件烦人的活儿。

jobber.t: n. 批发商；零工；股票批发商

e.en: The {jobber} buys in bulk and resells to small shops.
e.zh: 批发商大量进货,然后转售给小店。

e.en: He works as a freelance {jobber} for several construction firms.
e.zh: 他给几家建筑公司做自由零工。

jobbing.t:
adj. 打零工的
n. 零工活儿

e.en: He earns a living as a {jobbing} guitarist around town.
e.zh: 他在城里当个临时演出的吉他手谋生。

e.en: She hired a {jobbing} gardener to trim the hedges.
e.zh: 她请了个零工园丁来修剪树篱。

jobcentre.t: n. 就业中心（英国政府求职机构）

e.en: He visits the {jobcentre} every Friday to look for work.
e.zh: 他每周五去就业中心找工作。

e.en: The {jobcentre} runs free CV workshops on Tuesdays.
e.zh: 就业中心每周二举办免费的简历讲座。

e.en: He has been {jobless} since the factory closed last year.
e.zh: 自从去年工厂关闭以来,他一直失业。

e.en: The {jobless} rate dropped slightly last quarter.
e.zh: 上季度失业率略有下降。

e.en: Long-term {joblessness} can damage a person's mental health.
e.zh: 长期失业会损害一个人的心理健康。

e.en: The new policy aims to reduce youth {joblessness}.
e.zh: 这项新政策旨在降低青年失业率。

jobs.t: n. 工作（复数）；乔布斯（人名）

e.en: Many remote {jobs} now require strong communication skills.
e.zh: 现在许多远程工作都要求很强的沟通能力。

e.en: The factory closure cost the town hundreds of {jobs}.
e.zh: 工厂关闭使该镇失去了数百个工作岗位。

jock.t: n. 体育健将；运动型男生

e.en: He was the typical high school {jock}, popular and loud.
e.zh: 他是典型的高中运动男孩,人气高、嗓门大。

e.en: The radio {jock} took listener calls all morning.
e.zh: 那位电台主持人整个上午都在接听众电话。

jockey.t:
n. 赛马骑师
v. 钻营；操纵

e.en: The young {jockey} won her first big race today.
e.zh: 这位年轻的女骑师今天赢得了她的第一场大赛。

e.en: Reporters {jockey} for position outside the courtroom.
e.zh: 记者们在法庭外争抢有利位置。

jockeying.t: n. 暗中角逐；钻营争夺

e.en: The candidates are {jockeying} for the party's endorsement.
e.zh: 候选人们正在争夺党内的提名支持。

e.en: Cars were {jockeying} for space in the parking lot.
e.zh: 车辆在停车场里争抢车位。

e.en: He always wears a {jockstrap} during contact sports.
e.zh: 打对抗性运动时他总是穿运动护身。

e.en: The coach reminded players to pack a clean {jockstrap}.
e.zh: 教练提醒球员们带上一件干净的运动护身。

jocose.t: adj. 诙谐的；爱开玩笑的

e.en: His {jocose} remarks lightened the tense board meeting.
e.zh: 他诙谐的话语缓和了紧张的董事会气氛。

e.en: The professor had a surprisingly {jocose} lecturing style.
e.zh: 这位教授的讲课风格出人意料地诙谐。

jocular.t: adj. 爱开玩笑的；诙谐的

e.en: His {jocular} tone put the nervous interviewees at ease.
e.zh: 他幽默的语气让紧张的面试者放松下来。

e.en: The host made a {jocular} comment about the weather.
e.zh: 主持人就天气开了句玩笑。

e.en: Her natural {jocularity} made her the life of the party.
e.zh: 她天生爱开玩笑,成了派对的灵魂人物。

e.en: There was a forced {jocularity} in his voice that evening.
e.zh: 那晚他的声音里带着一种勉强的诙谐。

e.en: He {jocularly} blamed the dog for the missing cookies.
e.zh: 他开玩笑地把饼干不见的事赖到狗身上。

e.en: She {jocularly} called him the boss of the kitchen.
e.zh: 她打趣地叫他厨房的老大。

jocund.t: adj. 欢快的；愉悦的（文学用语）

e.en: The festival had a {jocund} atmosphere from start to finish.
e.zh: 这个节日从头到尾都洋溢着欢乐的气氛。

e.en: His {jocund} laughter filled the small wooden cabin.
e.zh: 他爽朗的笑声充满了那间小木屋。

jodhpur.t: n. 马裤；焦特布尔（印度城市）

e.en: She bought a pair of brown {jodhpur} pants for riding lessons.
e.zh: 她买了一条棕色的马裤上骑马课。

e.en: His tailor made a custom {jodhpur} jacket for the wedding.
e.zh: 他的裁缝为婚礼定做了一件马术风格的外套。

e.en: He {jokingly} called himself the world's worst cook.
e.zh: 他开玩笑地自称是世界上最差的厨师。

e.en: She {jokingly} suggested we move to Hawaii next year.
e.zh: 她开玩笑地提议我们明年搬去夏威夷。

joky.t: adj. 爱开玩笑的；戏谑的

e.en: His {joky} remarks lightened the tense meeting.
e.zh: 他诙谐的言语缓解了紧张的会议气氛。

e.en: She wrote a {joky} message in the birthday card.
e.zh: 她在生日贺卡上写了一段搞笑的话。

e.en: The party was full of music, food, and {jollity}.
e.zh: 派对上充满了音乐、美食和欢声笑语。

e.en: His warm laugh added to the {jollity} of the evening.
e.zh: 他爽朗的笑声为整个夜晚增添了欢乐。

jolly.t:
adj. 欢乐的；愉快的
adv. 非常

e.en: Santa is usually pictured as a {jolly} old man.
e.zh: 圣诞老人通常被描绘成一位快活的老人。

e.en: We had a {jolly} time at the family reunion.
e.zh: 我们在家庭聚会上玩得非常开心。

jolt.t:
v. 使颠簸；震惊
n. 颠簸；震动

e.en: The sudden brake caused a hard {jolt} in the car.
e.zh: 突然刹车让车里猛地颠了一下。

e.en: The bad news gave her quite a {jolt}.
e.zh: 那个坏消息让她大为震惊。

e.en: The bus ride was {jolting} along the unpaved road.
e.zh: 公共汽车在未铺设的路上颠簸前行。

e.en: Losing the contract was a {jolting} blow to the team.
e.zh: 失去那份合同对团队是个沉重的打击。

jonah.t: n. 约拿（圣经人物）；扫把星

e.en: In the Bible, {Jonah} was swallowed by a great fish.
e.zh: 圣经中，约拿被一条大鱼吞下。

e.en: The sailors called him a {jonah} after the storm.
e.zh: 那场暴风雨后，水手们都说他是个不祥之人。

e.en: A medieval {jongleur} entertained crowds with songs and tricks.
e.zh: 中世纪的吟游艺人用歌曲和杂技取悦人群。

e.en: The festival featured a {jongleur} juggling flaming torches.
e.zh: 节日上有一位吟游艺人表演抛接燃烧的火把。

e.en: A bright {jonquil} bloomed near the garden path.
e.zh: 一朵明黄的长寿花在花园小径旁绽放。

e.en: She painted the nursery a soft {jonquil} yellow.
e.zh: 她把婴儿房漆成了柔和的长寿花黄色。

e.en: Scott {Joplin} composed many famous ragtime piano pieces.
e.zh: 斯科特·乔普林创作了许多著名的拉格泰姆钢琴曲。

e.en: Janis {Joplin} remains one of rock's most iconic voices.
e.zh: 贾尼斯·乔普林至今仍是摇滚乐最具标志性的嗓音之一。

jordan.t: n. 约旦（国家）；乔丹（人名）

e.en: {Jordan} shares a long border with Saudi Arabia.
e.zh: 约旦与沙特阿拉伯有着漫长的边界。

e.en: Michael {Jordan} is widely considered basketball's greatest player.
e.zh: 迈克尔·乔丹被普遍认为是篮球史上最伟大的球员。

jordanian.t:
adj. 约旦的
n. 约旦人

e.en: The {Jordanian} dish was full of warm spices.
e.zh: 这道约旦菜满是温暖的香料风味。

e.en: My new neighbor is a {Jordanian} student studying engineering.
e.zh: 我的新邻居是一位学工程的约旦学生。

e.en: {Joseph} forgave his brothers in the famous Bible story.
e.zh: 在那个著名的圣经故事中，约瑟原谅了他的兄弟们。

e.en: My uncle {Joseph} runs a small bakery downtown.
e.zh: 我叔叔约瑟夫在市中心经营一家小面包店。

josh.t:
n. 乔什（男子名）
v. 开玩笑

e.en: Don't {josh} her — she's having a tough day.
e.zh: 别拿她开玩笑，她今天过得很糟。

e.en: The guys love to {josh} each other at the gym.
e.zh: 那些男生在健身房里特别爱互相调侃。

e.en: {Joshua} led the Israelites into the Promised Land.
e.zh: 约书亚带领以色列人进入了应许之地。

e.en: My son {Joshua} just started middle school this fall.
e.zh: 我儿子约书亚今年秋天刚上初中。

e.en: She lit a {joss} stick at the temple for good luck.
e.zh: 她在寺庙里点了一支香，祈求好运。

e.en: The smell of burning {joss} filled the small shrine.
e.zh: 烧香的气味弥漫在那座小神龛里。

e.en: Fans began to {jostle} for a better view of the stage.
e.zh: 粉丝们开始你推我挤，争抢更好的看台位置。

e.en: Commuters {jostle} each other on the crowded subway every morning.
e.zh: 通勤者每天早上在拥挤的地铁里互相推挤。

e.en: Reporters were {jostling} to ask the celebrity a question.
e.zh: 记者们你推我搡地想向那位名人提问。

e.en: Two startups are {jostling} for the top spot in the market.
e.zh: 两家初创公司正在争抢市场头名的位置。

jot.t:
v. 草草记下
n. 少量

e.en: Let me {jot} down your number before I forget it.
e.zh: 我趁还没忘，先把你的号码记下来。

e.en: She likes to {jot} ideas in a small notebook.
e.zh: 她喜欢把灵感随手记在小本子上。

e.en: He was {jotting} notes during the entire meeting.
e.zh: 整场会议他都在快速记笔记。

e.en: Her {jotting} in the margin became a brilliant essay.
e.zh: 她写在页边的随笔后来发展成一篇精彩文章。

e.en: One {joule} is the energy needed to lift a small apple one meter.
e.zh: 一焦耳大约相当于把一个小苹果举高一米所需的能量。

e.en: The battery stores millions of {joule} of electrical energy.
e.zh: 这块电池能储存数百万焦耳的电能。

jounce.t:
v. 颠簸；震动
n. 颠簸

e.en: The old truck began to {jounce} along the dirt road.
e.zh: 那辆旧卡车在土路上开始一路颠簸。

e.en: Every pothole made the stroller {jounce} violently.
e.zh: 每一个坑都让婴儿车剧烈颠动。

journal.t:
n. 日志；期刊
v. 写日记

e.en: She writes in her {journal} every night before bed.
e.zh: 她每晚睡前都会写日记。

e.en: The study was published in a top medical {journal}.
e.zh: 这项研究发表在一家顶级医学期刊上。

e.en: Daily {journaling} helps me manage anxiety and stay focused.
e.zh: 每天写日记帮助我缓解焦虑、保持专注。

e.en: Bullet {journaling} has become popular on social media.
e.zh: 子弹笔记法在社交媒体上越来越流行。

e.en: Investigative {journalism} exposed the company's hidden practices.
e.zh: 调查性新闻报道揭露了那家公司隐藏的做法。

e.en: She studied {journalism} at a top university in New York.
e.zh: 她在纽约一所顶尖大学攻读新闻学。

e.en: Different {journalisms} around the world face very different pressures.
e.zh: 世界各地不同的新闻业面临着差异极大的压力。

e.en: The book compares the {journalisms} of three Asian countries.
e.zh: 这本书比较了三个亚洲国家的新闻业。

e.en: The {journalist} interviewed survivors of the earthquake.
e.zh: 那位记者采访了地震的幸存者。

e.en: She became a freelance {journalist} after leaving the newspaper.
e.zh: 她离开报社后成了一名自由记者。

jodrell.t: n. 姓氏/地名 乔德雷尔

e.en: Astronomers at {Jodrell} Bank tracked the satellite all night.
e.zh: 卓瑞尔河岸天文台的天文学家整夜追踪那颗卫星。

e.en: We toured the famous {Jodrell} Bank radio telescope last summer.
e.zh: 我们去年夏天参观了著名的卓瑞尔河岸射电望远镜。

joe.t:
n. 男子名 乔
n. 咖啡（俚语）

e.en: I need a hot cup of {joe} before the meeting starts.
e.zh: 开会前我得喝杯热咖啡。

e.en: The average {Joe} can't afford a million-dollar home.
e.zh: 普通老百姓买不起百万美元的房子。

joey.t:
n. 人名 乔伊
n. 幼袋鼠

e.en: A baby kangaroo called a {joey} stays in the pouch.
e.zh: 小袋鼠叫做幼袋鼠，会待在育儿袋里。

e.en: The zoo announced that a new {joey} was born last week.
e.zh: 动物园宣布上周诞生了一只小袋鼠。

jog.t:
v. 慢跑
v. 轻推；唤起（记忆）

e.en: I {jog} in the park every morning before work.
e.zh: 我每天上班前都在公园里慢跑。

e.en: That photo might {jog} your memory of the trip.
e.zh: 那张照片或许能唤起你对那次旅行的记忆。

e.en: She {jogged} along the river for about an hour.
e.zh: 她沿着河边慢跑了大约一个小时。

e.en: His comment {jogged} my memory about the meeting.
e.zh: 他的话让我想起了那场会议。

jogger.t:
n. 慢跑者
n. 运动裤

e.en: A {jogger} waved at me as I walked the dog.
e.zh: 我遛狗时一位慢跑者向我挥手致意。

e.en: She bought new {jogger} pants for the gym.
e.zh: 她为去健身房买了一条新的运动裤。

jogging.t:
n. 慢跑
v. 慢跑（现在分词）

e.en: Daily {jogging} has really improved my sleep quality.
e.zh: 每天慢跑大大改善了我的睡眠质量。

e.en: He wore {jogging} shoes to the casual office party.
e.zh: 他穿着慢跑鞋去了那个轻松的办公室派对。

e.en: Her morning {joggings} around the lake became a daily ritual.
e.zh: 她每天清晨绕湖慢跑成了固定习惯。

e.en: Light {joggings} can help beginners build stamina gradually.
e.zh: 轻度慢跑有助于初学者逐步增强耐力。

e.en: Try not to {joggle} the table while I pour the wine.
e.zh: 我倒酒时请别晃动桌子。

e.en: The bumpy road made the cargo {joggle} in the truck.
e.zh: 颠簸的路面让卡车里的货物摇晃不停。

jogs.t: v. 慢跑（第三人称单数）

e.en: He {jogs} five kilometers every other morning.
e.zh: 他每隔一天清晨慢跑五公里。

e.en: Looking at old photos always {jogs} her memory.
e.zh: 看到旧照片总能唤起她的记忆。

johannesburg.t: n. 约翰内斯堡（南非城市）

e.en: {Johannesburg} is the largest city in South Africa.
e.zh: 约翰内斯堡是南非最大的城市。

e.en: Our flight to {Johannesburg} was delayed by three hours.
e.zh: 我们飞往约翰内斯堡的航班延误了三个小时。

e.en: The professor specializes in {Johannine} literature of the New Testament.
e.zh: 这位教授专攻新约中约翰著作的研究。

e.en: That metaphor reflects a distinctly {Johannine} theological style.
e.zh: 那个比喻反映出鲜明的约翰式神学风格。

john.t:
n. 男子名 约翰
n. 厕所（俚语）

e.en: {John} sent me an email about the project deadline.
e.zh: 约翰发邮件告诉我项目截止日期的事。

e.en: Excuse me, where's the nearest {john} in this restaurant?
e.zh: 请问，这家餐厅最近的洗手间在哪儿？

e.en: We rented a small {johnboat} for fishing on the lake.
e.zh: 我们租了一艘小平底船在湖上钓鱼。

e.en: A {johnboat} works well in shallow, calm waters.
e.zh: 平底小船在浅而平静的水域中很好用。

e.en: My grandfather used to enjoy a glass of {Johnnie} Walker.
e.zh: 我爷爷以前喜欢喝一杯尊尼获加威士忌。

e.en: {Johnnie} from accounting helped me fix the spreadsheet.
e.zh: 会计部的强尼帮我修好了那张电子表格。

johnny.t:
n. 男子名 约翰尼
n. 病号服

e.en: The nurse handed her a hospital {johnny} to change into.
e.zh: 护士递给她一件医院罩袍让她换上。

e.en: {Johnny} forgot to bring his lunch to school again.
e.zh: 约翰尼又忘了带午饭去学校。

e.en: All the public {johns} at the park were closed for cleaning.
e.zh: 公园里所有公共厕所都因清洁而关闭。

e.en: Two guys named {Johns} showed up to the interview.
e.zh: 两个都姓约翰斯的人来参加了面试。

johnsonian.t: adj. 约翰逊（博士）风格的

e.en: His writing style is admirably {Johnsonian} in its weight and wit.
e.zh: 他的文风庄重而机智，颇具约翰逊式风范。

e.en: The dictionary takes a {Johnsonian} approach to definitions.
e.zh: 这本词典在释义上采用了约翰逊式的方法。

join.t:
v. 加入；连接
n. 连接处

e.en: Would you like to {join} us for dinner tonight?
e.zh: 今晚要不要和我们一起吃晚饭？

e.en: Click the button to {join} the video meeting.
e.zh: 点击按钮即可加入视频会议。

e.en: She {joined} the company three months ago.
e.zh: 她三个月前加入了这家公司。

e.en: Thousands {joined} the protest in the city center.
e.zh: 数千人在市中心加入了抗议活动。

joiner.t:
n. 细木工
n. 爱加入组织的人

e.en: A skilled {joiner} built the custom kitchen cabinets.
e.zh: 一位手艺精湛的细木工打造了这套定制厨柜。

e.en: My sister is a real {joiner} at every social club.
e.zh: 我妹妹喜欢加入各种社交俱乐部。

joinery.t: n. 细木工活；接合工艺

e.en: The antique chair shows beautiful traditional {joinery}.
e.zh: 这把古董椅展示出精美的传统木工接合工艺。

e.en: Good {joinery} can last centuries without nails or glue.
e.zh: 出色的木工接合无需钉子或胶水也能保存几百年。

joining.t:
v. 加入（现在分词）
n. 连接处

e.en: Thanks for {joining} the call on such short notice.
e.zh: 感谢你在临时通知下还能加入这次通话。

e.en: She is considering {joining} a local hiking group.
e.zh: 她正考虑加入一个本地的徒步小组。

joins.t: v. 加入（第三人称单数）

e.en: He {joins} the team as our new lead designer.
e.zh: 他作为我们的新首席设计师加入团队。

e.en: This trail {joins} the main path near the waterfall.
e.zh: 这条小径在瀑布附近与主路汇合。

joint.t:
n. 关节；接头
adj. 共同的；联合的

e.en: My knee {joint} hurts after running long distances.
e.zh: 长跑之后我的膝关节就会痛。

e.en: The two countries issued a {joint} statement on trade.
e.zh: 两国就贸易问题发表了联合声明。

e.en: The book was {jointly} written by three researchers.
e.zh: 这本书由三位研究人员共同撰写。

e.en: They {jointly} own a small cafe downtown.
e.zh: 他们在市中心共同经营着一家小咖啡馆。

e.en: My {joints} ache whenever the weather turns cold.
e.zh: 每当天气转冷，我的关节就会酸痛。

e.en: This neighborhood has some great pizza {joints}.
e.zh: 这一带有几家很棒的披萨小店。

e.en: The contractor checked every floor {joist} for water damage.
e.zh: 承包商检查了每根地板托梁是否受潮损坏。

e.en: A wooden {joist} supports the weight of the ceiling.
e.zh: 一根木制托梁承托着天花板的重量。

jojoba.t: n. 荷荷巴（灌木及其籽油）

e.en: This shampoo contains {jojoba} oil to nourish dry hair.
e.zh: 这款洗发水含有荷荷巴油，可滋养干燥头发。

e.en: {Jojoba} is often used in natural skincare products.
e.zh: 荷荷巴常用于天然护肤产品中。

joke.t:
n. 笑话
v. 开玩笑

e.en: He told a {joke} that made everyone laugh out loud.
e.zh: 他讲了个笑话，把大家都逗得哈哈大笑。

e.en: Don't take it seriously — it was just a {joke}.
e.zh: 别当真，那只是个玩笑。

e.en: She {joked} that her cat runs the household.
e.zh: 她开玩笑说她家是猫在当家。

e.en: He {joked} about his terrible cooking skills.
e.zh: 他拿自己糟糕的厨艺开玩笑。

joker.t:
n. 大小王牌
n. 爱开玩笑的人

e.en: My brother is the {joker} of the family.
e.zh: 我弟弟是家里的开心果。

e.en: She drew the {joker} card and won the round.
e.zh: 她抽到了大王牌，赢下了这一局。

e.en: His {jokes} always lighten the mood at meetings.
e.zh: 他的笑话总能让会议气氛轻松起来。

e.en: She {jokes} with her coworkers during lunch breaks.
e.zh: 午休时她会和同事们开玩笑。

e.en: The office {jokester} hid everyone's mouse on April Fool's Day.
e.zh: 愚人节那天，办公室里的爱开玩笑的家伙把大家的鼠标都藏了起来。

e.en: Don't trust that {jokester} — he loves pranks.
e.zh: 别信那个爱开玩笑的家伙，他特别喜欢恶作剧。

jokey.t: adj. 爱开玩笑的；滑稽的

e.en: Her email had a {jokey} tone that made me smile.
e.zh: 她的邮件语气诙谐，让我会心一笑。

e.en: He gave a {jokey} answer instead of a serious one.
e.zh: 他没有正经回答，而是给了一个搞笑的答复。

joking.t:
v. 开玩笑（现在分词）
adj. 开玩笑的

e.en: Wait, are you {joking} or do you really mean it?
e.zh: 等等，你是开玩笑还是认真的？

e.en: Stop {joking} around and finish your homework.
e.zh: 别再开玩笑了，把作业做完。

journalistic.t: adj. 新闻业的；新闻工作者的

e.en: The article failed to meet basic {journalistic} standards.
e.zh: 这篇文章连最基本的新闻标准都达不到。

e.en: He has a clear, {journalistic} writing style.
e.zh: 他的文风清晰，颇具新闻报道的风格。

e.en: The piece is {journalistically} sound and well sourced.
e.zh: 这篇报道在新闻专业层面站得住脚，来源可靠。

e.en: She approached the topic {journalistically} rather than emotionally.
e.zh: 她以记者的方式而非情绪化的态度对待这个话题。

journalists.t: n. 记者；新闻工作者（复数）

e.en: Several {journalists} were waiting outside the courthouse.
e.zh: 几名记者在法院外等候。

e.en: Local {journalists} broke the story before national media did.
e.zh: 地方记者比全国媒体更早报道了这件事。

journals.t: n. 期刊；日志；日记（复数）

e.en: He keeps stacks of old {journals} from his college years.
e.zh: 他保留着大学时期一摞摞的旧日记本。

e.en: Many academic {journals} now publish articles online.
e.zh: 许多学术期刊现在把文章发布在网上。

journey.t:
n. 旅程；历程
v. 旅行

e.en: The {journey} from Beijing to Lhasa takes about two days by train.
e.zh: 从北京到拉萨坐火车大约要两天。

e.en: Learning a language is a long {journey}, not a quick task.
e.zh: 学一门语言是一段漫长旅程，而不是一蹴而就的事。

journeying.t:
v. 旅行（进行时）
n. 旅途

e.en: They spent the summer {journeying} across Southeast Asia.
e.zh: 他们整个夏天都在东南亚各地旅行。

e.en: She wrote a memoir about {journeying} alone through Africa.
e.zh: 她写了一本独自穿越非洲的旅行回忆录。

journeyman.t: n. 熟练工人；合格技工

e.en: He's a reliable {journeyman} actor in Hollywood films.
e.zh: 他是好莱坞电影里一名稳定可靠的二线演员。

e.en: After years as an apprentice, he became a {journeyman} carpenter.
e.zh: 做了多年学徒后，他成了一名熟练木匠。

journeys.t:
n. 旅程（复数）
v. 旅行（第三人称）

e.en: Her novels often follow the inner {journeys} of young women.
e.zh: 她的小说常常描写年轻女性的内心旅程。

e.en: Long train {journeys} are perfect for reading and napping.
e.zh: 长途火车旅行最适合看书和打盹。

journo.t: n. 记者（journalist 的口语缩写）

e.en: He's a veteran {journo} who has covered three wars.
e.zh: 他是个老记者，报道过三场战争。

e.en: A young {journo} broke the corruption scandal online.
e.zh: 一名年轻的小记者在网上爆出了那起腐败丑闻。

joust.t:
n. 骑士马上长矛比武
v. 较量；争斗

e.en: The two senators continue to {joust} over the new bill.
e.zh: 两位参议员仍在就新法案唇枪舌剑。

e.en: Knights in armor would {joust} for the queen's favor.
e.zh: 身披盔甲的骑士会为博得女王青睐而比武。

jousting.t:
n. 骑马持矛比武
v. 较量（进行时）

e.en: The candidates spent the debate {jousting} over tax policy.
e.zh: 两位候选人整场辩论都在就税收政策互相交锋。

e.en: Medieval {jousting} tournaments drew huge crowds.
e.zh: 中世纪的骑士比武大会吸引了大量观众。

e.en: By {Jove}, that was the best curry I've ever tasted!
e.zh: 天哪，那是我吃过最好吃的咖喱！

e.en: In Roman myth, {Jove} ruled the gods from Mount Olympus.
e.zh: 在罗马神话中，朱庇特从奥林匹斯山上统治众神。

e.en: Our neighbor is a {jovial} old man who loves telling jokes.
e.zh: 我们邻居是个爱讲笑话的快活老头。

e.en: The party had a warm and {jovial} atmosphere.
e.zh: 派对气氛温馨又欢快。

e.en: His {joviality} made everyone at the table relax.
e.zh: 他的爽朗让餐桌上每个人都放松下来。

e.en: There was a forced {joviality} to the office holiday party.
e.zh: 公司圣诞派对上有种刻意装出来的欢乐。

e.en: He {jovially} clapped his old friend on the back.
e.zh: 他乐呵呵地拍了拍老朋友的背。

e.en: The host greeted each guest {jovially} at the door.
e.zh: 主人在门口热情爽朗地迎接每位客人。

e.en: Astronomers studied the {Jovian} moons in great detail.
e.zh: 天文学家对木星的卫星进行了细致研究。

e.en: The probe captured stunning images of the {Jovian} atmosphere.
e.zh: 探测器拍下了木星大气层的惊艳影像。

e.en: The old bulldog had a saggy {jowl} and tired eyes.
e.zh: 那只老斗牛犬下巴松垂，眼神疲惫。

e.en: He rubbed his unshaven {jowl} and yawned.
e.zh: 他揉了揉没刮干净的下颌，打了个哈欠。

jowly.t: adj. 有双下巴的；颊肉下垂的

e.en: A {jowly} old judge presided over the courtroom.
e.zh: 一位双下巴松垂的老法官主持着庭审。

e.en: The portrait showed a {jowly} man in a dark suit.
e.zh: 画像中是一个穿深色西装、脸颊松垂的男人。

e.en: Her face lit up with {joy} when she saw the puppy.
e.zh: 看到那只小狗时，她脸上洋溢着喜悦。

e.en: Cooking for friends brings me real {joy}.
e.zh: 为朋友们下厨能给我带来真正的快乐。

joyce.t: n. 乔伊斯（人名，如作家 James Joyce）

e.en: James {Joyce} is famous for his novel Ulysses.
e.zh: 詹姆斯·乔伊斯以其小说《尤利西斯》闻名。

e.en: Many students struggle to read {Joyce} in the original.
e.zh: 许多学生读乔伊斯的原著都觉得吃力。

joycean.t: adj. 乔伊斯式的（指作家 Joyce 的风格）

e.en: The novel uses a {Joycean} stream-of-consciousness style.
e.zh: 这部小说采用了乔伊斯式的意识流写法。

e.en: Critics called the experimental film almost {Joycean} in ambition.
e.zh: 评论家说这部实验电影的野心几乎可比乔伊斯。

e.en: The wedding was a {joyful} celebration with friends and family.
e.zh: 那场婚礼是亲友们一起庆祝的欢乐时刻。

e.en: Children's laughter filled the park with a {joyful} sound.
e.zh: 孩子们的笑声让公园里充满欢乐的气息。

e.en: The dog ran {joyfully} toward its owner at the gate.
e.zh: 那只狗欢快地朝门口的主人跑去。

e.en: She {joyfully} accepted the job offer over the phone.
e.zh: 她在电话里欣喜地接受了这份工作邀请。

e.en: There was a quiet {joyfulness} in his voice that morning.
e.zh: 那天早上他的声音里透着一种安静的喜悦。

e.en: The song captures the simple {joyfulness} of childhood.
e.zh: 这首歌捕捉了童年那种单纯的欢乐。

joyless.t: adj. 毫无乐趣的；沉闷的

e.en: The office felt cold and {joyless} after the layoffs.
e.zh: 裁员之后，办公室显得冷清又毫无生气。

e.en: He described his childhood as strict and {joyless}.
e.zh: 他形容自己的童年既严苛又毫无乐趣。

joyous.t: adj. 充满喜悦的；欢乐的

e.en: The reunion was a {joyous} occasion for the whole family.
e.zh: 这次团聚对全家人来说都是一个欢乐的时刻。

e.en: A {joyous} cheer rose from the crowd at the final goal.
e.zh: 终场进球时，人群中爆发出欢呼声。

e.en: Children splashed {joyously} in the summer fountain.
e.zh: 孩子们在夏日的喷泉里尽情嬉水。

e.en: The choir sang {joyously} as the bride walked in.
e.zh: 新娘走进来时，唱诗班欢欣地高唱起来。

joyride.t:
n. 偷车兜风；飙车
v. 驾车兜风

e.en: Two teenagers took the car for a {joyride} last night.
e.zh: 两个青少年昨晚开走那辆车去兜风。

e.en: The whole road trip felt like one long {joyride}.
e.zh: 整趟公路旅行就像一场漫长的兜风。

e.en: Police arrested the {joyrider} after a short chase.
e.zh: 警方在短暂追逐后逮捕了那名偷车兜风的人。

e.en: A teenage {joyrider} crashed the stolen car into a fence.
e.zh: 一名飙车作乐的少年把偷来的车撞到了围栏上。

joyriding.t: n. 偷车兜风；疯狂飙车

e.en: The boys were caught {joyriding} in a stolen SUV.
e.zh: 那几个男孩开着一辆偷来的SUV兜风时被抓。

e.en: {Joyriding} is treated as a serious offense in many countries.
e.zh: 在许多国家，偷车兜风都被视为严重犯罪。

e.en: He gripped the {joystick} tightly during the dogfight scene.
e.zh: 在空战场景里他紧紧握着操纵杆。

e.en: This game feels much better with a {joystick} than a keyboard.
e.zh: 这款游戏用摇杆比用键盘体验好得多。

e.en: The dancers performed a lively {juba} on the porch.
e.zh: 舞者们在门廊上跳起了热闹的朱巴舞。

e.en: The drummer kept a steady beat for the {juba}.
e.zh: 鼓手为朱巴舞稳稳地打着节拍。

jubilant.t: adj. 喜气洋洋的；欢欣鼓舞的

e.en: Fans were {jubilant} after their team won the championship.
e.zh: 球队夺冠后，球迷们欣喜若狂。

e.en: She gave a {jubilant} speech upon receiving the award.
e.zh: 领奖时她发表了一段兴高采烈的致辞。

e.en: The crowd cheered {jubilantly} as fireworks lit the sky.
e.zh: 烟花点亮夜空时，人群欢呼雀跃。

e.en: He {jubilantly} announced the engagement on social media.
e.zh: 他在社交媒体上欣喜地宣布了订婚消息。

e.en: There was widespread {jubilation} when the war finally ended.
e.zh: 战争终于结束时，到处都是欢腾景象。

e.en: Her promotion was met with {jubilation} from the whole team.
e.zh: 她的晋升让整个团队都欢欣鼓舞。

e.en: The queen celebrated her diamond {jubilee} with a public parade.
e.zh: 女王以盛大的游行庆祝了她的钻石庆典。

e.en: The university held a {jubilee} to mark its 100th anniversary.
e.zh: 那所大学举办庆典庆祝建校一百周年。

judaea.t: n. 犹地亚（古代巴勒斯坦南部地区）

e.en: Roman governors ruled {Judaea} for several centuries.
e.zh: 罗马总督统治了犹地亚数百年。

e.en: The ancient region of {Judaea} appears often in the Bible.
e.zh: 古代的犹地亚地区在《圣经》中经常出现。

judah.t: n. 犹大（《圣经》人物；古以色列王国）

e.en: The kingdom of {Judah} survived after the fall of Israel.
e.zh: 以色列王国灭亡之后，犹大王国仍然延续。

e.en: In the Bible, {Judah} was one of Jacob's twelve sons.
e.zh: 《圣经》中，犹大是雅各十二个儿子之一。

judaic.t: adj. 犹太人的；犹太教的

e.en: She teaches a course on {Judaic} history and tradition.
e.zh: 她开设了一门犹太历史与传统的课程。

e.en: The museum has a rich collection of {Judaic} artifacts.
e.zh: 这家博物馆收藏了大量犹太文物。

e.en: {Judaism} is one of the world's oldest monotheistic religions.
e.zh: 犹太教是世界上最古老的一神教之一。

e.en: She converted to {Judaism} before her wedding last year.
e.zh: 她在去年婚礼前皈依了犹太教。

julienne.t:
n. 切成细丝的蔬菜
v. 把（菜）切成细丝

e.en: {Julienne} the carrots before adding them to the salad.
e.zh: 把胡萝卜切成细丝后再加入沙拉。

e.en: The salad came with {julienne} cucumber and bell peppers.
e.zh: 这道沙拉配有切丝的黄瓜和甜椒。

e.en: Romeo and {Juliet} remains Shakespeare's most famous tragedy.
e.zh: 《罗密欧与朱丽叶》仍是莎士比亚最著名的悲剧。

e.en: She played {Juliet} in the school's spring production.
e.zh: 她在学校春季演出中饰演朱丽叶。

e.en: We're going to Italy in {July} for two weeks.
e.zh: 我们七月份要去意大利两周。

e.en: Independence Day in America falls on {July} 4th.
e.zh: 美国的独立日是7月4日。

jumble.t:
n. 杂乱堆
v. 使混杂

e.en: My desk is a complete {jumble} of papers and cables.
e.zh: 我的桌子上文件和电线乱成一团。

e.en: Don't {jumble} the clean clothes with the dirty ones.
e.zh: 不要把干净衣服和脏衣服混在一起。

e.en: Her thoughts were {jumbled} after the long, exhausting flight.
e.zh: 漫长疲惫的飞行后,她的思绪一片混乱。

e.en: The drawer was full of {jumbled} cables and old chargers.
e.zh: 抽屉里塞满了缠在一起的电线和旧充电器。

e.en: I ordered a {jumbo} popcorn at the movie theater.
e.zh: 我在电影院点了一份超大份爆米花。

e.en: The {jumbo} jet can carry over 400 passengers comfortably.
e.zh: 这架巨型客机能舒适地搭载四百多名乘客。

jump.t:
v. 跳、跳跃
n. 跳跃；跳转

e.en: The cat tried to {jump} onto the kitchen counter.
e.zh: 那只猫试图跳上厨房台面。

e.en: Stock prices took a sudden {jump} after the announcement.
e.zh: 消息公布后股价突然飙升。

jumped.t: v. jump 的过去式，跳、跳跃

e.en: She {jumped} out of bed when the alarm rang.
e.zh: 闹钟一响她就从床上跳了起来。

e.en: Sales {jumped} thirty percent during the holiday season.
e.zh: 假期期间销售额猛增了百分之三十。

jumper.t:
n. 套头毛衣
n. 跳跃者

e.en: He wore a wool {jumper} to stay warm outside.
e.zh: 他穿着羊毛毛衣在外面保暖。

e.en: The high {jumper} cleared the bar on her first attempt.
e.zh: 那位跳高运动员第一次尝试就越过了横杆。

jumpers.t: n. jumper 的复数，套头毛衣

e.en: All the kids wore matching {jumpers} on picture day.
e.zh: 拍照那天孩子们都穿着同款的连衣裙。

e.en: You'll need {jumpers} to start the dead battery.
e.zh: 你需要电瓶搭线才能启动这块没电的电池。

jumping.t:
v. 跳跃（jump 的现在分词）
adj. 热闹的

e.en: The kids were {jumping} on the trampoline all afternoon.
e.zh: 孩子们整个下午都在蹦床上跳来跳去。

e.en: She keeps {jumping} from one project to another.
e.zh: 她总是从一个项目跳到另一个项目。

jumps.t: v./n. jump 的第三人称单数/复数

e.en: He {jumps} rope every morning before breakfast.
e.zh: 他每天早餐前都跳绳。

e.en: The video {jumps} whenever the connection gets weak.
e.zh: 信号一弱视频就会卡顿跳帧。

jumpstart.t:
v. 快速启动、助推启动
n. 应急启动

e.en: A morning coffee helps {jumpstart} my workday.
e.zh: 早晨一杯咖啡能帮我快速开启一天的工作。

e.en: The new tax break aims to {jumpstart} the economy.
e.zh: 新的减税政策旨在重振经济。

e.en: She wore a black {jumpsuit} to the cocktail party.
e.zh: 她穿着一身黑色连体裤参加鸡尾酒会。

e.en: Mechanics often wear a {jumpsuit} to keep their clothes clean.
e.zh: 机械工常穿连身工作服以保持衣服干净。

jumpy.t: adj. 神经紧张的、易受惊的

e.en: She gets {jumpy} whenever she drinks too much coffee.
e.zh: 她咖啡喝多了就会神经紧张。

e.en: The dog has been {jumpy} ever since the thunderstorm.
e.zh: 自从那场雷雨后这只狗就一直惊慌不安。

e.en: The report is due on {Jun} 15th this year.
e.zh: 报告将于今年六月十五日截止。

e.en: Her birthday falls on {Jun} 3rd every year.
e.zh: 她的生日是每年的六月三日。

e.en: Turn left at the next {junction} to reach the highway.
e.zh: 在下个路口左转就能上高速公路。

e.en: This town sits at the {junction} of two major rivers.
e.zh: 这个小镇坐落在两条大河的交汇处。

junctions.t: n. junction 的复数，交叉口

e.en: Traffic cameras monitor all major {junctions} in the city.
e.zh: 交通摄像头监控着市内所有主要路口。

e.en: Loose wires at the {junctions} caused the power outage.
e.zh: 接线处的松动电线导致了断电。

e.en: At this critical {juncture}, every decision matters.
e.zh: 在这个关键时刻,每个决定都至关重要。

e.en: The team faced a difficult {juncture} in the negotiations.
e.zh: 团队在谈判中遇到了艰难的关头。

e.en: We're planning a beach trip in early {June}.
e.zh: 我们打算六月初去海边旅行。

e.en: Roses bloom beautifully in our garden every {June}.
e.zh: 每年六月我们花园里的玫瑰都开得很美。

e.en: The last few {Junes} have been unusually rainy.
e.zh: 最近几年的六月雨水特别多。

e.en: She remembered the warm {Junes} of her childhood fondly.
e.zh: 她深情地回忆起童年那些温暖的六月。

jung.t: n. 荣格（瑞士心理学家）

e.en: Carl {Jung} developed the concept of the collective unconscious.
e.zh: 卡尔·荣格提出了集体无意识的概念。

e.en: My therapist often references {Jung} during our sessions.
e.zh: 我的治疗师在咨询中经常引用荣格的理论。

e.en: She practices {Jungian} analysis at her downtown clinic.
e.zh: 她在市中心的诊所从事荣格学派的心理分析。

e.en: The book offers a {Jungian} interpretation of fairy tales.
e.zh: 这本书从荣格学派的角度解读童话故事。

e.en: Wild monkeys swung through the dense {jungle} canopy.
e.zh: 野生猴子在茂密的丛林树冠间穿梭。

e.en: Navigating the city felt like surviving an urban {jungle}.
e.zh: 在这座城市穿行就像在城市丛林中求生。

e.en: The {jungles} of Borneo are home to rare orangutans.
e.zh: 婆罗洲的丛林里栖息着稀有的红毛猩猩。

e.en: Concrete {jungles} rarely offer real peace and quiet.
e.zh: 钢筋水泥的城市丛林难得有真正的宁静。

e.en: The backyard turned {jungly} after a month without mowing.
e.zh: 一个月没修剪,后院变得像丛林一样杂乱。

e.en: We hiked through the {jungly} hills outside the village.
e.zh: 我们徒步穿过村外那片丛林密布的山丘。

junior.t:
adj. 初级的、年少的
n. 下级；大三学生

e.en: She just got promoted from {junior} to senior developer.
e.zh: 她刚从初级开发者晋升为高级开发者。

e.en: My {junior} year of college was the most challenging.
e.zh: 大学三年级是我最具挑战性的一年。

e.en: Gin gets its distinctive flavor from {juniper} berries.
e.zh: 金酒独特的风味来自杜松子。

e.en: A row of {juniper} bushes lined the garden path.
e.zh: 一排杜松灌木沿着花园小径排列。

junk.t:
n. 废品、垃圾
v. 丢弃

e.en: My inbox is full of promotional {junk} every morning.
e.zh: 我的邮箱每天早上都塞满了垃圾推广邮件。

e.en: We cleaned out years of {junk} from the garage.
e.zh: 我们清理掉了车库里堆积多年的杂物。

junked.t: v. junk 的过去式，丢弃、报废

e.en: They {junked} the old car after the transmission failed.
e.zh: 变速箱坏了之后他们把那辆旧车报废了。

e.en: The team {junked} the original design and started over.
e.zh: 团队抛弃了最初的设计,从头开始。

e.en: He drives an old {junker} that barely passes inspection.
e.zh: 他开着一辆勉强能通过年检的破旧老爷车。

e.en: That bike is a total {junker}, not worth fixing.
e.zh: 那辆自行车彻底是堆破烂,不值得修了。

junkers.t: n. junker 的复数，破旧车

e.en: The lot was full of rusty {junkers} waiting to be scrapped.
e.zh: 停车场里满是等待报废的生锈破车。

e.en: Collectors sometimes restore old {junkers} into beautiful classics.
e.zh: 收藏家有时会把旧破车修复成漂亮的经典款。

junket.t: n. 公费旅游、游玩宴会

e.en: Reporters criticized the senator's expensive overseas {junket}.
e.zh: 记者们批评了那位参议员昂贵的公费海外旅行。

e.en: The press {junket} included interviews with the entire cast.
e.zh: 这次媒体宣传活动包括对全体演员的采访。

junkie.t: n. 瘾君子、狂热爱好者

e.en: He's a total fitness {junkie} who works out daily.
e.zh: 他是个十足的健身狂,每天都要锻炼。

e.en: Adventure {junkies} flock to this town for extreme sports.
e.zh: 极限运动爱好者纷纷涌向这个小镇追求刺激。

e.en: The old {junkman} pushed his cart down the alley.
e.zh: 那个收破烂的老人推着推车走过小巷。

e.en: A neighborhood {junkman} bought scrap metal from local residents.
e.zh: 小区里的废品收购员从居民那里收购废金属。

junks.t:
n. junk 的复数
n. 中式帆船

e.en: Traditional Chinese {junks} sailed through Hong Kong harbor at sunset.
e.zh: 传统中式帆船在日落时分驶过香港港口。

e.en: He {junks} every email that looks remotely promotional.
e.zh: 他把所有看起来像推广的邮件都当垃圾扔掉。

e.en: The drawer was filled with {junky} old cables and chargers.
e.zh: 抽屉里塞满了破旧的电线和充电器。

e.en: Don't waste money on that {junky} plastic toy.
e.zh: 别浪费钱买那种劣质的塑料玩具。

junkyard.t: n. 废品收购站、垃圾场

e.en: We found vintage car parts at the local {junkyard}.
e.zh: 我们在本地的废车场找到了一些古董车零件。

e.en: A guard dog patrolled the fenced-in {junkyard} at night.
e.zh: 一只看门狗夜里在围起来的废品场巡逻。

juno.t: n. 朱诺（罗马神话女神）

e.en: NASA's {Juno} spacecraft has been orbiting Jupiter since 2016.
e.zh: 美国宇航局的朱诺号飞船自2016年起一直在环绕木星运行。

e.en: In Roman mythology, {Juno} was the queen of the gods.
e.zh: 在罗马神话中,朱诺是众神之后。

junta.t: n. 军政府、军事执政团

e.en: The military {junta} seized power after the coup.
e.zh: 军政府在政变后夺取了政权。

e.en: International leaders condemned the {junta}'s human rights abuses.
e.zh: 国际领导人谴责了该军政府侵犯人权的行为。

e.en: Benjamin Franklin founded a {junto} to discuss civic improvements.
e.zh: 本杰明·富兰克林创立了一个讨论社区改良的小团体。

e.en: The local {junto} met weekly to debate political issues.
e.zh: 当地的这个小团体每周聚会讨论政治议题。

jupiter.t:
n. 木星
n. 朱庇特（罗马主神）

e.en: {Jupiter} is the largest planet in our solar system.
e.zh: 木星是太阳系中最大的行星。

e.en: You can spot {Jupiter} in the night sky tonight.
e.zh: 今晚你可以在夜空中看到木星。

e.en: We hiked through the scenic {Jura} mountains last summer.
e.zh: 去年夏天我们徒步穿越了风景秀丽的汝拉山脉。

e.en: The {Jura} region is famous for its distinctive wines.
e.zh: 汝拉地区以其独特的葡萄酒而闻名。

judas.t:
n. 犹大（圣经人物）
n. 叛徒

e.en: His best friend turned out to be a {Judas}.
e.zh: 他最好的朋友竟然是个叛徒。

e.en: The novel portrays him as a modern-day {Judas}.
e.zh: 这部小说把他描绘成现代版的犹大。

judder.t:
v. 剧烈抖动
n. 颤动

e.en: The old bus began to {judder} as it climbed the hill.
e.zh: 那辆旧巴士爬坡时开始剧烈震动。

e.en: I felt the steering wheel {judder} on the rough road.
e.zh: 我感到方向盘在颠簸路面上剧烈抖动。

juddering.t: v. 剧烈抖动（judder 的现在分词）

e.en: The {juddering} engine made everyone nervous during the flight.
e.zh: 飞行中震动不止的引擎让大家很紧张。

e.en: She felt a sudden {juddering} as the train braked hard.
e.zh: 火车急刹车时她感到一阵剧烈颤动。

e.en: My cousin {Jude} just moved to London for work.
e.zh: 我表弟裘德刚搬到伦敦工作。

e.en: The Beatles song "Hey {Jude}" remains a timeless classic.
e.zh: 披头士的《嘿,裘德》是一首永恒的经典。

judea.t: n. 犹地亚（古巴勒斯坦地区）

e.en: Ancient {Judea} was a province under Roman rule.
e.zh: 古代犹地亚曾是罗马统治下的一个行省。

e.en: The map shows the borders of historical {Judea} clearly.
e.zh: 这张地图清楚地显示了历史上犹地亚的边界。

judean.t:
adj. 犹地亚的
n. 犹地亚人

e.en: The museum displays many {Judean} coins from antiquity.
e.zh: 博物馆展出许多古代犹地亚的钱币。

e.en: Archaeologists discovered a {Judean} settlement near the Dead Sea.
e.zh: 考古学家在死海附近发现了一处犹地亚聚落。

judge.t:
n. 法官；评委
v. 判断

e.en: The {judge} sentenced him to five years in prison.
e.zh: 法官判处他五年监禁。

e.en: Don't {judge} a book by its cover.
e.zh: 不要以貌取人。

judged.t: v. 判断、评判（judge 的过去式）

e.en: The contest was {judged} by three industry experts.
e.zh: 比赛由三位业内专家担任评审。

e.en: She felt {judged} the moment she walked into the room.
e.zh: 她一走进房间就感到被人评头论足。

e.en: Trust your own {judgement} when making big decisions.
e.zh: 做重大决定时要相信自己的判断。

e.en: The court will deliver its {judgement} next Monday.
e.zh: 法院将于下周一作出判决。

judgemental.t: adj. 爱评判他人的；主观武断的

e.en: Try not to be so {judgemental} about her choices.
e.zh: 别对她的选择那么爱评头论足。

e.en: His {judgemental} tone made everyone uncomfortable at dinner.
e.zh: 他批判的语气让晚饭上的每个人都不自在。
